presquile.name: Presqu'ile
presquile.region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County
presquile.line: A family winery on a hill in the Santa Maria Valley, close enough to the Pacific to make cool, fresh Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Syrah.
presquile.tell: Presqu'ile farms its own vineyard in the Santa Maria Valley, where ocean fog keeps things cool. The wines are fresh and light on their feet: bright red fruited Pinot Noir, a dry Pinot rosé and a peppery Syrah. A good pick for a guest who wants California fruit without the weight.

martinelli.name: Martinelli
martinelli.line: A long established Sonoma farming family, known for ripe, generous Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Zinfandel from their own vineyards.
martinelli.tell: The Martinellis have farmed in the Russian River Valley for generations. Their style is ripe and generous, so Bella Vigne Pinot Noir is soft, round and full of dark cherry fruit. A friendly bottle for a guest who likes a plush red, and fair value on this list.

william-downie.name: William Downie
william-downie.line: An Australian winemaker known for light, pure, low intervention Pinot Noir from Victoria.
william-downie.tell: Bill Downie makes Pinot Noir in Victoria with very little intervention, aiming for lightness and perfume rather than power. Cathedral is fresh, bright and red fruited, a fun, gentle red that drinks beautifully slightly cool. Steer a Burgundy lover on a budget here.

chappellet.name: Chappellet
chappellet.line: A family estate that pioneered the rocky slopes of Pritchard Hill in Napa, making firm, long lived Cabernet.
chappellet.tell: Chappellet was one of the first to plant high on Pritchard Hill, east of the valley floor. The wines are dark and structured. Mountain Cuvée is the friendly, approachable blend; Signature is the classic Cabernet; Pritchard Hill is the estate's flagship, built to age.

duckhorn.name: Duckhorn
duckhorn.line: The Napa house that made Merlot famous in California, now also known for polished Cabernet; Three Palms is its celebrated Merlot vineyard.
duckhorn.tell: Duckhorn made its name with Merlot when few in Napa took it seriously. Three Palms Vineyard Merlot is the famous one: plush, plummy and deep. The Napa Cabernet is smooth and reliable. A safe, recognisable name, and the large bottles suit a big table.

division-winemaking.name: Division Winemaking Company
division-winemaking.line: An urban winery in Portland making lively, Loire and Beaujolais inspired wines from Oregon vineyards.
division-winemaking.tell: Division is a small Portland winery that takes its cue from the Loire and Beaujolais. Renardière is Gamay from the Eola-Amity Hills: juicy, bright and lightly peppery, lovely a touch cool. A great pick for a guest who wants a light red with fish or poultry.

pride-mountain.name: Pride Mountain Vineyards
pride-mountain.line: A family estate high on Spring Mountain whose vineyards straddle the Napa and Sonoma county line, known for dense Merlot and Cabernet.
pride-mountain.tell: Pride sits right on the county line at the top of Spring Mountain, so some rows are in Napa and some in Sonoma. Mountain fruit gives deep, concentrated wines. The Merlot is rich and dark, more powerful than most, and the half bottle suits two guests.

andrew-geoffrey.name: Andrew Geoffrey Vineyards
andrew-geoffrey.line: A small hillside estate high on Diamond Mountain, making Cabernet Sauvignon from volcanic soils.
andrew-geoffrey.tell: Andrew Geoffrey farms a small vineyard high on Diamond Mountain, above Calistoga, on pale volcanic soil. The Cabernet is firm and concentrated, with dark currant fruit and a herbal edge. The half bottle is a handy way to give two guests a mountain Napa Cabernet.

bergstrom.name: Bergstrom
bergstrom.line: A family estate in the northern Willamette Valley, farming biodynamically and known for rich, layered Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
bergstrom.tell: Bergstrom is a family winery in Oregon's Willamette Valley, farmed biodynamically. Their Pinot Noirs are deep and silky, with more richness than many Oregon wines. Le Pré du Col and Shea are single vineyards, Silice comes from sandy soils, and Reserve blends the best barrels.

bethel-heights.name: Bethel Heights
bethel-heights.line: A family estate and one of the early names in the Eola-Amity Hills, making fresh, balanced Oregon Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
bethel-heights.tell: Bethel Heights is a family estate that has farmed the Eola-Amity Hills for decades. Afternoon winds from the coast keep the wines fresh. The Pinot Noir is bright and red fruited, with fine acidity, and the half bottle is perfect for one or two guests with fish or duck.

diamond-creek.name: Diamond Creek
diamond-creek.line: A Diamond Mountain pioneer that bottles its Cabernet by vineyard: Volcanic Hill, Red Rock Terrace and Gravelly Meadow.
diamond-creek.tell: Diamond Creek was among the first in Napa to bottle each vineyard separately, so guests can compare. Volcanic Hill is the firmest, Red Rock Terrace the most fragrant, Gravelly Meadow fine and mineral. These are long lived mountain Cabernets; older vintages need a word with the sommelier and a decanter.

goldeneye.name: Goldeneye
goldeneye.line: Duckhorn's Pinot Noir estate in the cool Anderson Valley of Mendocino, making rich, polished Pinot.
goldeneye.tell: Goldeneye is the Pinot Noir home of the Duckhorn family, in the foggy Anderson Valley north of Sonoma. The wine is ripe and generous, with dark cherry and a silky texture. A good choice for a Cabernet drinker trying Pinot for the first time; also in half bottle and magnum.

hartford-court.name: Hartford Court
hartford-court.line: A Sonoma winery focused on cool climate Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and old vine Zinfandel from the Russian River Valley and beyond.
hartford-court.tell: Hartford Court makes Pinot Noir from cool sites in Sonoma and Mendocino. The Russian River Valley bottling is ripe and silky, with red cherry and a little spice, an easy crowd pleaser. The half bottle suits two guests; Muldane Trail comes from Anderson Valley.

ken-wright.name: Ken Wright Cellars
ken-wright.line: A Willamette Valley winery known for single vineyard Pinot Noirs that show how each site differs.
ken-wright.tell: Ken Wright helped Oregon think vineyard by vineyard. Shea, Canary Hill, McCrone, Carter and Freedom Hill are separate bottlings from different hills and soils, so a guest can taste the difference. The style is fresh and fruit led; the half bottles and magnums give real choice by table size.

kosta-browne.name: Kosta Browne
kosta-browne.line: A Sonoma Pinot Noir house famous for ripe, plush, polished wines that many California Pinot lovers seek out.
kosta-browne.tell: Kosta Browne makes Pinot Noir in a ripe, lush style: dark cherry, spice and a velvety texture. The Sonoma Coast and Russian River bottlings are the core; Gap's Crown is a single vineyard in the windy Petaluma Gap. A sure pick for a guest who loves rich California Pinot.

la-crema.name: La Crema
la-crema.line: A well known Sonoma winery making approachable, fruit forward Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from cool coastal vineyards.
la-crema.tell: La Crema is one of the names guests recognise for California Pinot Noir. The Sonoma Coast bottling is soft and fruity, with cherry and a touch of vanilla, easy with almost anything. A safe, friendly choice, and the half bottle is good value for two.

opus-one.name: Opus One
opus-one.line: The Oakville estate created by Robert Mondavi and Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Mouton, making one Bordeaux style blend; Overture is its second wine.
opus-one.tell: Opus One began as a partnership between Robert Mondavi and the Rothschilds of Château Mouton. It makes one wine, a Cabernet led blend, polished and long lived. Overture is the estate's second wine. Guests know the name; the list holds half bottles up to a six litre Imperial.

ridge.name: Ridge Vineyards
ridge.line: A historic California winery famous for Monte Bello Cabernet from the Santa Cruz Mountains and for old vine Zinfandel blends from Sonoma.
ridge.tell: Ridge is one of the great names of California. Monte Bello, from high in the Santa Cruz Mountains, is a firm, long lived Cabernet blend. Lytton Springs, Pagani Ranch and Three Valleys are Zinfandel based: spicy, brambly and generous. Essence is a sweet late harvest wine for dessert.

shafer.name: Shafer Vineyards
shafer.line: A family estate in the Stags Leap District whose Hillside Select Cabernet is one of the most sought after in Napa.
shafer.tell: Shafer is a Napa family winery on the slopes of the Stags Leap District. Hillside Select is the famous Cabernet: rich, velvety and long. One Point Five is the more approachable Cabernet, Relentless a Syrah blend, and the Merlot is plush and polished.

starmont.name: Starmont
starmont.line: The Carneros label of the family that owns Merryvale, best known for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, with a Napa red here in half bottle.
starmont.tell: Starmont grew out of Merryvale in St. Helena and now makes its wines at Stanly Ranch in Carneros. It is a dependable, fairly priced label. The Napa Valley red here is a half bottle, a sensible pick for one or two guests; ask the sommelier which grapes are in it.

au-bon-climat.name: Au Bon Climat
au-bon-climat.region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County
au-bon-climat.line: The Santa Barbara winery founded by Jim Clendenen, which championed balanced, Burgundy style Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in California.
au-bon-climat.tell: Au Bon Climat helped put Santa Barbara on the map with fresh, balanced wines in the Burgundy mould. The Pinot Noirs, like Isabelle, Knox Alexander and La Bauge au Dessus, are bright and savoury rather than heavy. Hildegard is a richer white blend. A smart choice for a guest who likes Burgundy.

mayacamas.name: Mayacamas Vineyards
mayacamas.line: A historic stone winery high on Mount Veeder, famous for lean, long lived Cabernet and Chardonnay made without heavy oak.
mayacamas.tell: Mayacamas sits near the top of Mount Veeder, above the fog. The Cabernet is firm and restrained, made to age for decades rather than to impress young, and the list holds a run of vintages. The Chardonnay is lean and fresh. Ideal for a guest who prefers classic, less oaky Napa.

hirsch-vineyards.name: Hirsch Vineyards
hirsch-vineyards.line: A pioneering vineyard on the ridges of the far Sonoma Coast, near the Pacific, making taut, fragrant Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
hirsch-vineyards.tell: Hirsch farms steep ridges a few miles from the ocean on the far Sonoma Coast. The Pinot Noirs are fresh, savoury and fine, closer to Burgundy than to ripe California. East Ridge, West Ridge and San Andreas Fault are separate parts of the estate. Lovely with salmon, duck or mushrooms.

araujo.name: Araujo (Eisele Vineyard)
araujo.line: The estate built on the Eisele Vineyard near Calistoga, one of the historic great Cabernet sites of Napa.
araujo.tell: Eisele Vineyard, near Calistoga, has been famous for Cabernet for decades, and Araujo made it a cult name. The wine is deep, structured and fine, built to age. This magnum is a celebration bottle; involve the sommelier for decanting and service.

arcadian.name: Arcadian
arcadian.line: A Central Coast winery making restrained, Burgundy minded Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, often released with some age.
arcadian.tell: Arcadian makes Pinot Noir in a quiet, Burgundian way, picking for freshness and often holding wines back before release. Expect red fruit, earth and a silky texture rather than power. The magnum of Francesca is a good bottle for a table that loves Pinot.

belle-glos.name: Belle Glos
belle-glos.region: Sonoma Coast and Santa Maria Valley
belle-glos.line: A Pinot Noir label from the family behind Caymus, known for ripe, dark, generous single vineyard wines.
belle-glos.tell: Belle Glos is the Pinot Noir side of the Wagner family of Caymus, and the style matches: ripe, dark fruited and plush. Taylor Lane comes from the Sonoma Coast. A great Pinot for a guest who usually drinks Napa Cabernet; here in magnum for a big table.

bond.name: BOND
bond.line: The Harlan family's project bottling Cabernet from single hillside vineyards: Melbury, Quella, St. Eden, Vecina and Pluribus.
bond.tell: BOND comes from the family behind Harlan Estate. Each wine is Cabernet from one hillside site: St. Eden and Vecina are dark and powerful, Melbury and Quella more perfumed, Pluribus from Spring Mountain. Rare, costly bottles across several vintages; decant and involve the sommelier.

cade.name: Cade
cade.line: A Howell Mountain estate from the PlumpJack group, making powerful mountain Cabernet from volcanic soils.
cade.tell: Cade is the PlumpJack family winery up on Howell Mountain, above the Napa Valley fog. Mountain fruit gives a dark, firm Cabernet with plenty of structure. The estate magnum is a strong, generous bottle for a table eating steak.

canvasback.name: Canvasback
canvasback.line: Duckhorn's Washington State winery, making Cabernet Sauvignon from the warm, small Red Mountain area.
canvasback.tell: Canvasback is the Duckhorn family in Washington. Red Mountain is a warm, dry corner of the state that gives dark, firm Cabernet with good freshness. A smart pick for a Napa drinker who wants something different at a fair price; here in magnum.

caymus.name: Caymus
caymus.line: A Wagner family winery in Rutherford, famous for rich, velvety Napa Cabernet; Special Selection is the top wine.
caymus.tell: Caymus is one of the best known Napa names. The style is ripe, round and velvety, with dark fruit and soft tannin, easy to enjoy young. Special Selection is the richer flagship, and the 50th Anniversary bottling comes in a three litre double magnum.

clos-du-val.name: Clos du Val
clos-du-val.line: One of the early Stags Leap District wineries, founded with a French winemaker and known for balanced, elegant Cabernet.
clos-du-val.tell: Clos du Val was among the first wineries in the Stags Leap District and has always aimed for balance over power. The Cabernets are polished and food friendly. Hirondelle is their estate vineyard, Three Graces the top blend; the many vintages and magnums give plenty of choice.

copain.name: Copain
copain.line: A California winery known for restrained, fresh Pinot Noir, Syrah and Chardonnay from cool vineyards.
copain.tell: Copain picks early for freshness, making wines in a restrained, European style. Kiser is a Pinot Noir vineyard in the Anderson Valley, bright and fragrant, here in magnum. Tous Ensemble Syrah is peppery and lively. A good pick for guests who want lighter California reds.

elk-cove.name: Elk Cove
elk-cove.line: A family estate among the older wineries of the Willamette Valley, known for Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris.
elk-cove.tell: Elk Cove is a family winery in the northern Willamette Valley. Roosevelt Vineyard is one of their single sites: a darker, deeper Pinot Noir with fine tannin. The list holds several vintages in magnum, a good way to bring an Oregon Pinot to a big table.

faust.name: Faust
faust.line: A Napa Cabernet label from the Huneeus family of Quintessa, ripe and polished in style.
faust.tell: Faust comes from the family behind Quintessa. It is a ripe, generous Napa Cabernet, with dark fruit and smooth tannin, easy to like. Here in magnum, it is a strong value choice for a table that wants big Napa red.

jordan.name: Jordan
jordan.line: A Sonoma estate in the Alexander Valley making one Cabernet in an elegant, food friendly style inspired by Bordeaux.
jordan.tell: Jordan is a famous Sonoma name with a quieter style than most Napa Cabernet: medium bodied, fresh and balanced, made to go with food. Guests often know it from restaurants. The magnum and double magnum suit a celebration table.

joseph-phelps.name: Joseph Phelps
joseph-phelps.line: A leading Napa estate whose Insignia was one of the first proprietary Bordeaux style blends in California.
joseph-phelps.tell: Joseph Phelps makes classic Napa Cabernet. Insignia, the flagship blend, is rich, layered and long lived, and it is one of the best known Napa reds. The list holds it from half bottle to magnum and across vintages. The Napa Valley Cabernet is the easier entry.

heitz-cellar.name: Heitz Cellar
heitz-cellar.line: A historic Napa winery whose Martha's Vineyard Cabernet is among California's most famous single vineyard wines.
heitz-cellar.tell: Heitz made one of Napa's first famous single vineyard Cabernets, Martha's Vineyard, often described with a minty, eucalyptus note. Trailside and Linda Falls are other sites. The list holds a long run of vintages; for older ones, ask the sommelier how they are drinking and decant gently.

daou.name: DAOU
daou.line: A Paso Robles winery founded by two brothers, making rich, Bordeaux style reds on the hills west of town; Patrimony is the top wine.
daou.tell: DAOU farms steep limestone hills west of Paso Robles. The wines are ripe, dark and polished. Caves des Lions and Soul of a Lion are Cabernet led, and Patrimony is the flagship, here also in magnum. A good choice for a guest who loves rich Napa style red.

plumpjack.name: PlumpJack
plumpjack.line: An Oakville estate making ripe, polished Cabernet, the founding winery of a group that includes Cade and Odette.
plumpjack.tell: PlumpJack sits in Oakville, the heart of Napa Cabernet country. The Estate Cabernet is rich and supple, with dark fruit and fine tannin. The magnum is a good bottle for a table of four or more with steak.

quintessa.name: Quintessa
quintessa.line: A biodynamically farmed estate in Rutherford owned by the Huneeus family, making one elegant Cabernet led blend.
quintessa.tell: Quintessa is a single estate in Rutherford, farmed biodynamically, that makes one blended red. It is polished and fine rather than heavy, with dark fruit and a long finish. The three litre bottle here is for a big celebration; plan it with the sommelier.

radio-coteau.name: Radio-Coteau
radio-coteau.line: A Sonoma winery making cool climate Syrah, Pinot Noir and Zinfandel with a light hand and real freshness.
radio-coteau.tell: Radio-Coteau farms and buys from cool coastal sites in western Sonoma. The Syrahs are peppery and savoury, Las Colinas and Timbervine among them, and Lemorel is a fresh, elegant Zinfandel. A great choice for a guest who likes Northern Rhône wines.

spottswoode.name: Spottswoode
spottswoode.line: A family estate in St. Helena, farmed organically, known for elegant, long lived Cabernet; Lyndenhurst is its second wine.
spottswoode.tell: Spottswoode is a family estate on the western edge of St. Helena, farmed organically. The Estate Cabernet is graceful and fine, more about balance than power, and it ages very well. Lyndenhurst is the more approachable second wine. Several vintages and magnums are on the list.

trefethen.name: Trefethen
trefethen.line: A family estate in the cool Oak Knoll District of southern Napa, making balanced Cabernet, blends and a Malbec blend.
trefethen.tell: Trefethen is a family estate in Oak Knoll, one of Napa's cooler corners, so the reds stay fresh. The Estate Cabernet is balanced and food friendly; Halo is the top Cabernet; Dragon's Tooth is a dark, spicy Malbec blend and Eshcol a Bordeaux style blend.

kistler.name: Kistler
kistler.line: A Sonoma estate famous for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir made in a Burgundian way from cool vineyards.
kistler.tell: Kistler is one of the great Chardonnay names of California, and its Pinot Noir is made with the same care. The Sonoma Coast Pinot is fine and fragrant, with red fruit and a silky texture. A strong choice for a guest who wants California Pinot with finesse.

lioco.name: Lioco
lioco.line: A California winery making restrained, fresh wines from cool vineyards, with little new oak.
lioco.tell: Lioco makes California wine that stays fresh and light on oak. The Pinot Noir from Comptche, in the cool hills of Mendocino, is bright and savoury, with red fruit and spice. A smart pick for a guest who finds most California Pinot too heavy.

maggy-hawk.name: Maggy Hawk
maggy-hawk.line: An Anderson Valley estate in Mendocino's cool 'deep end', making silky, aromatic single vineyard Pinot Noir.
maggy-hawk.tell: Maggy Hawk farms an estate in the far, cool end of the Anderson Valley, named for a racehorse. Jolie is elegant and silky, with bright raspberry and floral notes. A lovely Pinot for salmon, duck or a guest who wants something fine but not heavy.

dumol.name: DuMOL
dumol.line: A Russian River Valley winery known for rich yet fresh Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Syrah from cool Sonoma sites.
dumol.tell: DuMOL makes Pinot Noir in the Russian River Valley with ripe fruit and good freshness. Ryan and Wester Reach are vineyard bottlings, dark cherried and silky. A good choice for a guest who likes a fuller Pinot that still tastes lively.

hanzell.name: Hanzell
hanzell.line: One of the oldest Pinot Noir and Chardonnay estates in California, in the hills above the Sonoma Valley, built in homage to Burgundy.
hanzell.tell: Hanzell was set up long ago to make Burgundy style wine in Sonoma and still farms some of the oldest Pinot Noir vines in the state. The Pinot is firm, savoury and long lived, not a fruit bomb. A classic, collectable California name; decant younger bottles.

kalin-cellars.name: Kalin Cellars
kalin-cellars.line: A small California winery that holds its wines for years before release, so bottles arrive with maturity and layers.
kalin-cellars.tell: Kalin Cellars is known for patience: wines are aged for years before they are sold. Cuvée DD is a Pinot Noir from the Alexander Valley, so expect mature, earthy, layered flavours rather than fresh fruit. Ask the sommelier how the vintage is drinking.

marcassin.name: Marcassin
marcassin.line: Winemaker Helen Turley's tiny estate on the far Sonoma Coast, one of California's most sought after names for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
marcassin.tell: Marcassin is a tiny estate on the far Sonoma Coast made famous by winemaker Helen Turley. The Pinot Noir is rich and concentrated, and bottles are hard to find. A collector's wine; involve the sommelier for service and any questions about the vintage.

schrader.name: Schrader Cellars
schrader.line: A Napa label famous for powerful Cabernets from the Beckstoffer To Kalon Vineyard in Oakville, with Pinot Noir under the Boar's View name.
schrader.tell: Schrader is known for Cabernet from Beckstoffer To Kalon, one of Napa's most famous vineyards. The wines are dark, rich and polished; T6 and RBS are named for particular clones and blocks. Boar's View is a Pinot Noir from the far Sonoma Coast. Celebration bottles; decant.

stout.name: Stout Vineyards
stout.line: A small California family producer bottling Pinot Noir and Cabernet in limited amounts.
stout.tell: Stout is a small family label. This list carries a Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir and a Napa Valley Cabernet. They are made in small amounts, so ask the sommelier about the style of each before you describe them to a guest.

brick-and-mortar.name: Brick & Mortar
brick-and-mortar.line: A small California producer making single vineyard wines in limited amounts, here a Napa Valley Pinot Noir.
brick-and-mortar.tell: Brick & Mortar is a small producer working with single vineyards. Cougar Rock Vineyard Pinot Noir comes from Napa, unusual for a grape usually grown in cooler spots. Ask the sommelier about its weight and style before you recommend it.

calera.name: Calera
calera.line: A Central Coast pioneer that planted Pinot Noir on the limestone of remote Mount Harlan, the soil of Burgundy.
calera.tell: Calera went looking for limestone, like Burgundy, and found it high on Mount Harlan. Its single vineyard Pinot Noirs, Jensen, Mills, Reed and Ryan, are fresh, fine and long lived, each a little different. A favourite for guests who love Burgundy. Doux is a sweet Viognier for dessert.

cambria.name: Cambria
cambria.region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County
cambria.line: A Santa Maria Valley estate making cool climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; Julia's Vineyard is its best known Pinot.
cambria.tell: Cambria farms the cool, foggy Santa Maria Valley. Julia's Vineyard Pinot Noir is bright and red fruited, with a little spice, approachable and fairly priced. An easy, friendly California Pinot for poultry or salmon.

domaine-de-la-cote.name: Domaine de la Côte
domaine-de-la-cote.region: Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Barbara County
domaine-de-la-cote.line: A Sta. Rita Hills estate of densely planted vineyards near the ocean, making taut, Burgundy minded single vineyard Pinot Noir.
domaine-de-la-cote.tell: Domaine de la Côte farms windy, cool hillsides at the western edge of the Sta. Rita Hills. The Pinot Noirs are fresh, savoury and fine, nearer Burgundy than ripe California. Bloom's Field, La Côte, Memorious and Sirens Call are separate sites. Great with duck, salmon or mushrooms.

folktale.name: Folktale Winery
folktale.line: A Carmel Valley winery blending Monterey County fruit, with literary names on its wines.
folktale.tell: Folktale is a Carmel Valley winery with storybook names. The Ruler is a Pinot Noir blended from several Monterey County sites, including the Santa Lucia Highlands: earthy, savoury and full. A good, generous Pinot for heartier dishes.

the-hilt.name: The Hilt
the-hilt.region: Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Barbara County
the-hilt.line: A Sta. Rita Hills estate making cool climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from vineyards swept by Pacific wind.
the-hilt.tell: The Hilt farms in the Sta. Rita Hills, where the ocean wind keeps the grapes cool. The Pinot Noir is bright and fine, with red fruit, spice and fresh acidity. A strong choice for a guest who likes elegant Pinot with salmon or duck.

antica-terra.name: Antica Terra
antica-terra.line: An Eola-Amity Hills estate known for intense, perfumed Pinot Noir made in very small amounts.
antica-terra.tell: Antica Terra farms a steep, rocky site in the Eola-Amity Hills. Its Pinot Noirs are layered and fragrant, with real depth; Obelin is one of its named cuvées. Rare and much admired. A treat for a Pinot lover; ask the sommelier about the vintage.

cristom.name: Cristom
cristom.line: A family estate in the Eola-Amity Hills known for single vineyard Pinot Noirs, several named for family members.
cristom.tell: Cristom farms its own hills in the Eola-Amity area and bottles vineyards separately. Paul Gerrie Vineyard is named for the founder: a dark, spicy, structured Pinot Noir. A fine Oregon choice for duck or lamb.

evening-land.name: Evening Land Vineyards
evening-land.line: An Eola-Amity Hills winery built around the Seven Springs vineyard, known for taut, mineral Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
evening-land.tell: Evening Land farms Seven Springs, one of Oregon's most respected vineyards. Summum is the top selection: a fine, intense Pinot Noir with real structure. A strong pick for a Burgundy drinker who wants to try Oregon.

moonflower.name: Moonflower
moonflower.line: A small Willamette Valley label making organically farmed estate Pinot Noir in the northern part of the valley.
moonflower.tell: Moonflower is a small Oregon label with organically farmed estate fruit from the north of the Willamette Valley. The Pinot Noir is light, bright and savoury, with raspberry and a little earth. A gentle, fresh red for fish or poultry.

soter.name: Soter Vineyards
soter.line: An Oregon estate founded by winemaker Tony Soter, built around the Mineral Springs Ranch vineyard.
soter.tell: Soter farms Mineral Springs Ranch in the Yamhill-Carlton area of the Willamette Valley. The Pinot Noir is dark fruited, silky and polished. Here in half bottle, a good Oregon choice for one or two guests.

eyrie.name: The Eyrie Vineyards
eyrie.line: The winery that planted the first Pinot Noir in the Willamette Valley in the 1960s, still family run and making light, graceful wines.
eyrie.tell: Eyrie is where Oregon Pinot Noir began. Original Vines comes from those first plantings; South Block and Sisters are other old sites. The wines are pale, fragrant and fine, and age beautifully. They also make a rare Pinot Meunier. A must for a guest who loves history and finesse.

zena-crown.name: Zena Crown
zena-crown.line: An Eola-Amity Hills vineyard estate making structured Pinot Noir from its own blocks.
zena-crown.tell: Zena Crown farms a single hillside estate in the Eola-Amity Hills. The Sum is the estate blend and Conifer a block selection: dark fruited, firm and fresh Pinot Noir. Good with duck, pork or mushrooms.

amuse-bouche.name: Amuse Bouche
amuse-bouche.line: A small Napa winery making a Merlot led, Pomerol style blend, created with winemaker Heidi Barrett.
amuse-bouche.tell: Amuse Bouche was set up with Heidi Barrett, a celebrated Napa winemaker, to make a Pomerol style red: Merlot with Cabernet Franc. It is plush, round and dark fruited. A great choice for a guest who loves Merlot or Right Bank Bordeaux.

bacio-divino.name: Bacio Divino
bacio-divino.line: A Napa winery whose Janzen label bottles single vineyard Cabernets from famous Beckstoffer sites.
bacio-divino.tell: Bacio Divino makes its Janzen Cabernets from Beckstoffer vineyards: To Kalon in Oakville and Missouri Hopper. The style is rich, ripe and opulent, with dark fruit and spice. A strong choice for a guest who wants big Napa Cabernet with a famous vineyard name.

beaulieu-vineyard.name: Beaulieu Vineyard
beaulieu-vineyard.line: A historic Rutherford estate; its Georges de Latour Private Reserve is one of Napa's benchmark Cabernets.
beaulieu-vineyard.tell: Beaulieu, called BV, is one of the old names of Napa. Georges de Latour Private Reserve, named for the founder, has been a benchmark Rutherford Cabernet for generations: dark fruit, cedar and the dusty earthiness Rutherford is known for.

burgess.name: Burgess Cellars
burgess.line: A long standing Napa winery on the hillsides above St. Helena, making classic, balanced Cabernet.
burgess.tell: Burgess has worked the hillsides above St. Helena for decades. The Reserve Cabernet is classic and balanced, with dark fruit and firm structure. A good traditional Napa choice for beef.

cardinale.name: Cardinale
cardinale.line: A Napa estate blending Cabernet from mountain and valley vineyards into one polished, powerful wine.
cardinale.tell: Cardinale blends Cabernet from mountain and valley floor vineyards across Napa into one wine. It is dark, polished and long, built for steak and for celebration. The list holds several vintages; ask the sommelier which is drinking best tonight.

chateau-montelena.name: Chateau Montelena
chateau-montelena.line: A historic Calistoga estate, famous since its Chardonnay won the 1976 Paris tasting, and known for long lived Estate Cabernet.
chateau-montelena.tell: Montelena's Chardonnay beat top white Burgundy at the 1976 Paris tasting, a great story at the table. Its Estate Cabernet, from the foot of Mount St. Helena, is firm, classic and long lived. A traditional Napa pick for beef.

chimney-rock.name: Chimney Rock
chimney-rock.line: A Stags Leap District winery making supple, elegant Cabernet from estate vineyards.
chimney-rock.tell: Chimney Rock farms the Stags Leap District, known for soft, silky Cabernet often called an iron fist in a velvet glove. The Estate Cabernet is polished, with dark cherry and fine tannin. A good classic Napa pick.

continuum.name: Continuum
continuum.line: The Mondavi family estate on Pritchard Hill, run by Tim Mondavi, making one Cabernet led blend.
continuum.tell: Continuum is the next chapter of the Mondavi family, on rocky Pritchard Hill above the valley. It makes one wine, a Cabernet led blend with Cabernet Franc: deep, structured and fine. The list holds many vintages; ask the sommelier which is ready.

dalla-valle.name: Dalla Valle
dalla-valle.line: A family estate on the Oakville hillside, famous for its estate Cabernet and for Maya, a Cabernet and Cabernet Franc blend.
dalla-valle.tell: Dalla Valle sits on the eastern hills of Oakville. Its Cabernet is rich and firm, and Maya, blended with Cabernet Franc, is one of Napa's most sought after wines. Celebration bottles; decant and give them time in the glass.

darioush.name: Darioush
darioush.line: A Napa estate with a winery inspired by ancient Persia, making rich, polished Cabernet.
darioush.tell: Darioush is a Napa winery whose founder drew on his Persian heritage for its striking building. The Cabernet is ripe, plush and polished, with dark fruit and soft tannin. A crowd pleaser for steak.

david-arthur.name: David Arthur
david-arthur.line: A family estate on Pritchard Hill making concentrated mountain Cabernet.
david-arthur.tell: David Arthur is a family winery on the rocky slopes of Pritchard Hill. Old Vines Cabernet is concentrated and firm, with dark fruit and mountain structure. A good choice with beef or lamb.

dominus.name: Dominus Estate
dominus.line: Christian Moueix's Napa estate near Yountville, making a refined, Bordeaux minded Cabernet blend.
dominus.tell: Dominus belongs to Christian Moueix, whose family is famous in Pomerol. The wine comes from the old Napanook vineyard near Yountville and is fine, firm and less showy than many Napa reds. A great choice for a Bordeaux lover.

forman.name: Forman Vineyard
forman.line: Winemaker Ric Forman's small Napa estate, known for restrained, Bordeaux style Cabernet and lean Chardonnay.
forman.tell: Ric Forman makes a small amount of Cabernet in a restrained, Bordeaux like style: medium bodied, fresh and made to age. A thoughtful pick for a guest who wants classic Napa without heavy oak. Several vintages are on the list.

freemark-abbey.name: Freemark Abbey
freemark-abbey.line: A historic St. Helena winery and an early champion of single vineyard Cabernet, notably Bosché and Sycamore.
freemark-abbey.tell: Freemark Abbey is one of the old names of Napa. Bosché and Sycamore were among the first vineyard named Cabernets in California: classic, cedary and long lived. The Napa Valley Cabernet is the easier entry.

frogs-leap.name: Frog's Leap
frogs-leap.line: A Rutherford winery farming organically without irrigation, making balanced, food friendly Cabernet, Merlot and Zinfandel.
frogs-leap.tell: Frog's Leap farms organically and dry farms its vines in Rutherford. The wines are balanced and lower in alcohol than many Napa reds: the Cabernet is fresh and savoury, the Merlot supple. A good pick for a guest who wants Napa that goes with food.

grgich-hills.name: Grgich Hills
grgich-hills.line: The estate of Mike Grgich, who made the winning 1976 Paris Chardonnay at Montelena, now farming organically across Napa.
grgich-hills.tell: Grgich Hills was founded by Mike Grgich, the winemaker behind the Chardonnay that won the 1976 Paris tasting. The estate farms organically. The Cabernet is balanced and classic, the Zinfandel spicy, and Violetta is a sweet late harvest wine for dessert.

harlan-estate.name: Harlan Estate
harlan-estate.line: The Oakville hillside estate of Bill Harlan, one of the most celebrated and costly Cabernets in America.
harlan-estate.tell: Harlan Estate farms the western hills of Oakville and makes one of Napa's most famous Cabernet blends: deep, layered and very long lived. The list holds many vintages. These are trophy bottles; involve the sommelier, decant and give it time.

heritance.name: Heritance
heritance.line: A Napa label of the Taub family, making classic Cabernet from mid valley sites such as Beckstoffer Georges III in Rutherford.
heritance.tell: Heritance bottles Napa Cabernet in a classic style. Georges III is a famous Beckstoffer vineyard in Rutherford, once part of the Beaulieu holdings, and gives a rich, dark wine with Rutherford's dusty earthiness. A good value way to a famous vineyard name.

hourglass.name: Hourglass
hourglass.region: St. Helena and Calistoga, Napa Valley
hourglass.line: A family estate in the narrow north of Napa Valley, making dark, polished Cabernet and blends.
hourglass.tell: Hourglass takes its name from the shape of the valley where it narrows near St. Helena. The Estate Cabernet is dark, rich and smooth, with good freshness. A strong modern Napa choice for steak.

hundred-acre.name: Hundred Acre
hundred-acre.line: A cult Napa winery making very ripe, opulent single vineyard Cabernets such as Ark, Kayli Morgan and Wraith.
hundred-acre.tell: Hundred Acre makes Cabernet in a big, opulent style: very ripe, dense and velvety. Ark, Kayli Morgan and Wraith are separate vineyards. Rare and costly; for a guest who loves the richest Napa, and a bottle to decant.

hyde-de-villaine.name: Hyde de Villaine
hyde-de-villaine.line: A partnership between the Hyde family of Carneros and Aubert de Villaine of Burgundy's Romanée-Conti, making elegant wines.
hyde-de-villaine.tell: Hyde de Villaine joins a Carneros farming family with Aubert de Villaine of Burgundy. Belle Cousine is their Merlot led red blend: fresh, fine and restrained, California fruit with European balance. A thoughtful pick for a Bordeaux lover.

ink-grade.name: Ink Grade
ink-grade.line: A Howell Mountain estate making Cabernet from high, rocky vineyards.
ink-grade.tell: Ink Grade farms on Howell Mountain, high above the Napa fog. Mountain Cabernet here is dark, firm and concentrated. A strong pick for beef; ask the sommelier about decanting.

j-davies.name: J. Davies
j-davies.line: The red wine estate of the Davies family of Schramsberg, making Cabernet on Diamond Mountain.
j-davies.tell: J. Davies is the Cabernet side of the family behind Schramsberg sparkling wine, from their vineyards on Diamond Mountain. The wine is structured and dark, with mountain firmness. A nice story if the table started with Schramsberg.

jarvis.name: Jarvis
jarvis.line: A Napa estate known for its winery built entirely inside caves, making rich Cabernet.
jarvis.tell: Jarvis makes its wine inside a network of caves in the hills east of Napa. The Reserve Cabernet is rich and long, with dark fruit and polish. A good celebratory Napa pick.

kongsgaard.name: Kongsgaard
kongsgaard.line: A small Napa family winery famous for its Chardonnay, also making deep Syrah and Cabernet.
kongsgaard.tell: Kongsgaard is best known for Chardonnay, but its reds are just as serious. The Syrah is dark, savoury and peppery, the Cabernet deep and firm. Small production; a collector's choice.

la-jota.name: La Jota
la-jota.line: A historic Howell Mountain winery making dark, firm mountain Cabernet and Merlot.
la-jota.tell: La Jota is an old stone winery on Howell Mountain. Mountain fruit gives a dark, firm Cabernet and a structured Merlot with more grip than most. Both suit beef or lamb.

lail.name: Lail Vineyards
lail.line: The winery of Robin Lail, from the family that founded Inglenook; J. Daniel Cuvée Cabernet honours her father.
lail.tell: Lail comes from one of Napa's oldest wine families, descended from the founders of Inglenook. J. Daniel Cuvée is a refined, long lived Cabernet named for Robin Lail's father. Elegant and classic.

larkmead.name: Larkmead
larkmead.line: A historic Calistoga estate making elegant Cabernet blends and Merlot from its own vineyard.
larkmead.tell: Larkmead is an old estate at the north end of Napa. Dr. Olmo and The Lark are its Cabernet led blends, elegant and long; Firebelle is a Merlot blend. A refined choice for a guest who likes balance.

lokoya.name: Lokoya
lokoya.line: A Napa winery bottling mountain Cabernets, one from each of the valley's mountain areas.
lokoya.tell: Lokoya makes separate Cabernets from Napa's mountains: Howell Mountain, Spring Mountain, Mount Veeder and Diamond Mountain. Each is dark, powerful and distinct. Rare bottles; a fine comparison for a serious Cabernet lover.

merryvale.name: Merryvale
merryvale.line: A family owned St. Helena winery; Profile is its flagship Cabernet led blend.
merryvale.tell: Merryvale is a family winery in St. Helena. Profile, the flagship, is a Cabernet led blend: rich, layered and polished. A classic Napa choice for steak.

odette.name: Odette
odette.line: A Stags Leap District estate in the PlumpJack group, making polished Cabernet.
odette.tell: Odette is the PlumpJack family's winery in the Stags Leap District, where Cabernet tends to be supple and silky. The Napa Cabernet is dark, smooth and polished. A good choice for a guest who likes soft, rich red.

paul-hobbs.name: Paul Hobbs
paul-hobbs.line: A celebrated California winemaker bottling rich single vineyard Cabernet in Napa, alongside projects in Argentina.
paul-hobbs.tell: Paul Hobbs is one of California's best known winemakers. Beckstoffer Dr. Crane, in St. Helena, and Nathan Coombs, in Coombsville, are single vineyard Cabernets: ripe, dark and plush. He also founded Viña Cobos in Argentina, also on this list.

peter-michael.name: Peter Michael
peter-michael.line: An estate in the volcanic hills of Knights Valley known for Les Pavots, a Bordeaux style blend, and rich Chardonnay.
peter-michael.tell: Peter Michael farms steep volcanic slopes in Knights Valley. Les Pavots is the estate blend: deep, fine and long lived. L'Esprit des Pavots is the younger drinking version, and Au Paradis comes from Oakville in Napa. A celebration name; several vintages are listed.

pilcrow.name: Pilcrow
pilcrow.line: A small Napa label that began with Cabernet from the Pym Rae vineyard on Mount Veeder.
pilcrow.tell: Pilcrow is a small label whose first wines came from the Pym Rae vineyard high on Mount Veeder. Mountain Cabernet here is dark and firm, with black fruit and a floral note. Ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

pym-rae.name: Pym-Rae
pym-rae.line: A Mount Veeder estate bought by the Tesseron family of Château Pontet-Canet, bottled under its own name.
pym-rae.tell: Pym-Rae is a hillside estate on Mount Veeder, now owned by the family behind Château Pontet-Canet in Pauillac. The Cabernet is firm and fine, mountain fruit made with a Bordeaux sensibility. A thoughtful pick for a Bordeaux drinker.

ramey.name: Ramey Wine Cellars
ramey.line: A Sonoma winery best known for Chardonnay, also making Bordeaux style reds from Napa and the North Coast.
ramey.tell: Ramey is a leading Sonoma Chardonnay house that also makes serious red. Pedregal is a single vineyard Cabernet from Oakville, dark and structured; Claret is the friendlier North Coast blend.

robert-foley.name: Robert Foley Vineyards
robert-foley.line: A Howell Mountain winery making bold, structured mountain reds.
robert-foley.tell: Robert Foley makes wine high on Howell Mountain. The Cabernet is bold and dark, with the firm grip mountain fruit gives. A strong choice with beef; decant if it is young.

robert-mondavi.name: Robert Mondavi Winery
robert-mondavi.line: The Oakville winery that did more than any to make Napa famous; its Reserve Cabernet comes from the To Kalon Vineyard.
robert-mondavi.tell: Robert Mondavi built Napa's reputation around the world. The Reserve Cabernet comes from To Kalon, one of the most famous vineyards in America: rich, structured and long lived. A classic name for a celebration.

round-pond.name: Round Pond Estate
round-pond.line: A family estate in Rutherford making balanced Cabernet from its own vineyards.
round-pond.tell: Round Pond is a family estate on the valley floor in Rutherford. The Estate Cabernet is balanced and smooth, with dark cherry and a touch of earth. A friendly, fairly priced Napa choice.

second-line.name: Second Line Wines
second-line.line: A small Napa label with New Orleans roots; Big Chief Cabernet honours the city's Mardi Gras Indian tradition.
second-line.tell: Second Line is a small Napa label with a New Orleans heart: Big Chief is named for the leaders of the Black Masking Indian tribes who parade at Mardi Gras. It is a dark, full Napa Cabernet. A wonderful story to tell a visitor at Brennan's.

sequoia-grove.name: Sequoia Grove
sequoia-grove.line: A Rutherford winery making classic Napa Cabernet, including single vineyard bottlings.
sequoia-grove.tell: Sequoia Grove is a Rutherford winery named for its grove of redwoods. Tonella is a single vineyard Cabernet: dark, rich and classic, with Rutherford's dusty earthiness. A solid steak wine.

silver-oak.name: Silver Oak
silver-oak.line: A winery that makes only Cabernet, aged in American oak, in Napa Valley and Alexander Valley versions.
silver-oak.tell: Silver Oak makes Cabernet only, aged in American oak, which gives a soft texture and notes of vanilla and coconut. The Alexander Valley bottling is rounder and friendlier, the Napa Valley one firmer. Guests often ask for it by name.

snowden.name: Snowden
snowden.line: A small Napa family label making Cabernet from family vineyards.
snowden.tell: Snowden is a small family producer. Brothers Vineyard is a single site Cabernet: dark and structured. Small production, so ask the sommelier about style and readiness.

spring-mountain-vineyard.name: Spring Mountain Vineyard
spring-mountain-vineyard.line: A historic estate on the slopes of Spring Mountain above St. Helena, making long lived mountain Cabernet.
spring-mountain-vineyard.tell: Spring Mountain Vineyard farms steep hillsides above St. Helena. The Cabernet is firm and fresh, with mountain structure and the ability to age. Several vintages are on the list; a classic choice with beef.

staglin.name: Staglin Family Vineyard
staglin.line: A family estate on the Rutherford Bench, making refined Cabernet from organically farmed vines.
staglin.tell: Staglin is a family estate on the Rutherford Bench, one of Napa's classic Cabernet strips. The wine is refined and long, with dark fruit and Rutherford's earthy note. A strong celebration choice.

stags-leap-wine-cellars.name: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars
stags-leap-wine-cellars.line: The winery whose Cabernet won the 1976 Paris tasting; Cask 23 is its flagship.
stags-leap-wine-cellars.tell: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars made the Cabernet that beat top Bordeaux at the 1976 Paris tasting. Cask 23 is the flagship: silky, perfumed and long. Ne Cede Malis is a rare old vine field blend. A great story for the table.

textbook.name: Textbook
textbook.line: A Napa label making Cabernet that aims for restraint, with Mise en Place from two Oakville sites.
textbook.tell: Textbook makes Napa Cabernet in a restrained style. Mise en Place, French for everything in its place, comes from two Oakville vineyards: polished and fine. The Reserve is the step up. A kitchen word a guest at Brennan's will enjoy.

the-mascot.name: The Mascot
the-mascot.line: A Cabernet from the Harlan family, made from the younger vines of their estates.
the-mascot.tell: The Mascot comes from the family behind Harlan Estate and BOND, made from younger vines on their properties. It is dark, polished and approachable sooner. The best value way to the Harlan family's style.

turnbull.name: Turnbull Wine Cellars
turnbull.line: An Oakville winery making classic Napa Cabernet from estate vineyards.
turnbull.tell: Turnbull farms vineyards in Oakville and beyond. Black Label is its top Cabernet: rich, dark and structured. A classic Napa steak wine.

ulysses.name: Ulysses
ulysses.line: Christian Moueix's Oakville estate, making a refined Cabernet blend.
ulysses.tell: Ulysses is the Oakville estate of Christian Moueix, of Pomerol fame and Dominus. The wine is fine and balanced, with Bordeaux like restraint. A thoughtful pick for a guest who loves classic Bordeaux.

anakota.name: Anakota
anakota.line: A Knights Valley estate making powerful mountain Cabernet from volcanic hillsides.
anakota.tell: Anakota farms volcanic hillsides in Knights Valley, between Napa and Sonoma. The Cabernets are dark, firm and concentrated; Helena Montana is a single vineyard. Good with beef; decant if young.

les-lunes.name: Les Lunes
les-lunes.line: A small natural wine label that farms organically and makes wines with as little intervention as it can.
les-lunes.tell: Les Lunes is a small label making natural wine from vineyards it farms organically. The Sonoma Cabernet is lighter and fresher than most, with bright fruit and an earthy edge. A fun pick for an adventurous guest.

stonestreet.name: Stonestreet
stonestreet.line: An estate with high mountain vineyards above the Alexander Valley, making powerful Cabernet and Chardonnay.
stonestreet.tell: Stonestreet farms steep vineyards high above the Alexander Valley. The Cabernet is ripe and powerful, kept fresh by altitude. A strong Sonoma choice for beef.

verite.name: Vérité
verite.line: A Sonoma estate making three Bordeaux style blends: La Muse led by Merlot, La Joie by Cabernet and Le Désir by Cabernet Franc.
verite.tell: Vérité makes Bordeaux style wine from Sonoma hillsides. La Muse is Merlot led and plush, La Joie Cabernet led and firm, Le Désir Cabernet Franc led and fragrant. Rare and celebrated; several vintages are listed, and a good choice for a Bordeaux collector.

kathryn-kennedy.name: Kathryn Kennedy Winery
kathryn-kennedy.line: A small estate in Saratoga in the Santa Cruz Mountains, making long lived Cabernet from its own vineyard.
kathryn-kennedy.tell: Kathryn Kennedy is a tiny estate in the Santa Cruz Mountains. The Estate Cabernet is firm, fresh and long lived, in a classic style. Older vintages are listed; ask the sommelier how they are drinking.

steven-kent.name: Steven Kent Winery
steven-kent.line: A Livermore Valley winery making Bordeaux style reds; Lineage is its flagship blend.
steven-kent.tell: Steven Kent makes wine in the Livermore Valley, east of San Francisco, one of California's oldest wine areas. Lineage is a Cabernet led blend, dark and polished. An interesting alternative to Napa.

andrew-will.name: Andrew Will
andrew-will.line: A respected Washington winery making Bordeaux style blends from Columbia Valley vineyards.
andrew-will.tell: Andrew Will makes blends in the Bordeaux style from Washington vineyards. Sorella, from Horse Heaven Hills, is the flagship: Cabernet led, structured and fine. A good choice for a Bordeaux lover who wants something new.

quilceda-creek.name: Quilceda Creek
quilceda-creek.line: A family winery whose Columbia Valley Cabernet is among Washington's most celebrated.
quilceda-creek.tell: Quilceda Creek is a family winery and Washington's most famous Cabernet name. The wine is rich, dense and polished, with dark fruit and great length. Several vintages are listed; a celebration bottle.

bedrock.name: Bedrock Wine Co.
bedrock.line: A Sonoma winery devoted to old vineyards, known for field blends, Zinfandel and Syrah.
bedrock.tell: Bedrock works with some of California's oldest vineyards. The Syrah is peppery and savoury, with dark fruit. A great choice for a guest who likes Rhône wines.

charles-smith.name: Charles Smith
charles-smith.line: A Washington winemaker known for bold labels and dark, powerful Syrah; Royal City is his top Syrah.
charles-smith.tell: Charles Smith is a showman of Washington wine. Royal City is his flagship Syrah: dark, dense and meaty, with smoke and pepper. For a guest who loves big reds.

ex-post-facto.name: Ex Post Facto
ex-post-facto.line: A Syrah project from Santa Barbara winemaker Greg Brewer, whole cluster fermented and aged in old barrels.
ex-post-facto.tell: Ex Post Facto is Greg Brewer's Syrah, from cool Santa Barbara County. It is made with whole bunches and no new oak, so it is peppery, floral and fresh. A smart pick for a Northern Rhône lover.

haynes-vineyard.name: Haynes Vineyard
haynes-vineyard.line: A vineyard estate in cool Coombsville, Napa, making fresh, low oak Syrah and Pinot Noir.
haynes-vineyard.tell: Haynes Vineyard sits in Coombsville, one of Napa's coolest corners. Forgeron is a Syrah made with whole bunches and old barrels: floral, peppery and fresh. Unusual for Napa, and lovely with lamb or duck.

hudson-vineyards.name: Hudson Vineyards
hudson-vineyards.line: A famous Carneros grower whose fruit goes to many top wineries, also bottling its own wines.
hudson-vineyards.tell: Hudson is a renowned grower in Carneros whose grapes appear on many famous labels. Its own Syrah is cool climate in style: dark fruit, pepper and fresh acidity. Good with lamb.

jonata.name: Jonata
jonata.line: An estate in Ballard Canyon, Santa Barbara County, making rich, intense reds.
jonata.tell: Jonata farms sandy hills in Ballard Canyon. Todos is an estate red blend: ripe, dark and spicy. Ask the sommelier for the exact grape mix of the vintage.

martin-woods.name: Martin Woods
martin-woods.line: A small Oregon winery making fresh, precise single vineyard wines.
martin-woods.tell: Martin Woods is a small Oregon producer. Rockbar Vineyard Syrah comes from The Rocks District, a stony area known for savoury, meaty Syrah. A great choice for a guest who likes Rhône wines.

peay.name: Peay Vineyards
peay.line: A family estate on the far Sonoma Coast making cool climate Syrah, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
peay.tell: Peay farms one of the coolest spots in California, close to the ocean on the far Sonoma Coast. Les Titans Syrah is peppery, savoury and fresh, closer to the Northern Rhône than to ripe California.

piedrasassi.name: Piedrasassi
piedrasassi.line: A small Santa Barbara producer making savoury, fresh Syrah from single vineyards.
piedrasassi.tell: Piedrasassi makes Syrah in a fresh, savoury style. Bien Nacido, in the Santa Maria Valley, and Rim Rock, in Arroyo Grande, are cool sites: pepper, dark fruit and lively acidity. Great with lamb or duck.

tenshen.name: Tenshen
tenshen.line: A Santa Barbara County label best known for Rhône style blends.
tenshen.tell: Tenshen makes blends in Santa Barbara County, built mainly on Rhône grapes such as Syrah and Grenache. Expect ripe, spicy, dark fruit. Ask the sommelier for the blend of this bottle.

alexander-valley-vineyards.name: Alexander Valley Vineyards
alexander-valley-vineyards.line: A family estate in the Alexander Valley making approachable, fairly priced reds.
alexander-valley-vineyards.tell: Alexander Valley Vineyards is a long standing family estate in northern Sonoma. The Merlot is soft and plummy, easy to enjoy. Here in half bottle, a good value pick for one or two guests.

keenan.name: Keenan Winery
keenan.line: A Spring Mountain estate known for structured mountain Merlot, Cabernet Franc and blends.
keenan.tell: Keenan farms high on Spring Mountain. Mailbox Vineyard is its celebrated Merlot, deep and firm; Upper Bowl is a Cabernet Franc, and Holy Trinity a blend. Mountain wines with more grip than valley versions.

orin-swift.name: Orin Swift
orin-swift.line: A California winery known for bold labels and rich, ripe blends.
orin-swift.tell: Orin Swift is famous for striking labels and generous wines. Advice From John is a Merlot led blend: ripe, round and full. A crowd pleaser for a guest who likes rich red.

broc-cellars.name: Broc Cellars
broc-cellars.line: An urban winery in Berkeley making light, natural style wines from organically farmed vineyards.
broc-cellars.tell: Broc Cellars is a Berkeley winery making natural wines. Vine Starr Zinfandel is lighter and fresher than most, juicy and bright. A fun choice for a guest who wants a gentle red.

frank-family.name: Frank Family Vineyards
frank-family.line: A Napa winery in Calistoga making approachable Cabernet, Zinfandel and Chardonnay.
frank-family.tell: Frank Family is a popular Napa name with an easygoing style. The Zinfandel is ripe and spicy, with jammy berry fruit, a good partner for barbecue flavours or a rich, peppery dish.

ancient-oak-cellars.name: Ancient Oak Cellars
ancient-oak-cellars.line: A small family winery in Sonoma working with family vineyards, known for Cabernet Franc.
ancient-oak-cellars.tell: Ancient Oak is a small family winery in Sonoma. Alcaeus is a Cabernet Franc based blend from Sonoma Mountain: red and black fruit, herbs and fine tannin. A thoughtful pick for a guest who likes Loire or Right Bank reds.

lang-and-reed.name: Lang & Reed
lang-and-reed.line: A small winery devoted to Cabernet Franc.
lang-and-reed.tell: Lang & Reed specialises in Cabernet Franc, a grape usually used only for blending in California. Two Fourteen is fresh and fragrant, with red fruit and herbs. A great choice for a guest who loves Chinon or Saumur.

dunn.name: Dunn Vineyards
dunn.line: A family estate on Howell Mountain famous for firm, long lived Cabernet in a restrained style.
dunn.tell: Dunn makes some of Napa's longest lived reds, high on Howell Mountain: firm, dark and less alcoholic than many. Young bottles are tight and need decanting. Ask the sommelier about this one, which the list groups with Petite Sirah.

clendenen-family.name: Clendenen Family Vineyards
clendenen-family.region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County
clendenen-family.line: Jim Clendenen's personal label, made alongside Au Bon Climat, with Italian grapes such as Nebbiolo.
clendenen-family.tell: Clendenen Family is the personal label of Jim Clendenen of Au Bon Climat, where he worked with Italian grapes. Punta Exclamativa is a Nebbiolo from the Santa Maria Valley: perfumed, firm and savoury. A fun swap for a Barolo lover.

mount-brave.name: Mount Brave
mount-brave.line: A Mount Veeder estate making mountain reds, including an unusual Malbec.
mount-brave.tell: Mount Brave farms steep slopes on Mount Veeder. Its Malbec is dark, dense and firm, with mountain structure. An unusual Napa red for a guest who likes Argentinian Malbec.

screaming-eagle.name: Screaming Eagle
screaming-eagle.line: One of Napa's most famous cult estates in Oakville; Second Flight is its second wine.
screaming-eagle.tell: Screaming Eagle is perhaps the most famous cult wine in California, made in tiny amounts in Oakville. Second Flight is its second wine, still rare and costly. A trophy bottle; involve the sommelier.

the-prisoner.name: The Prisoner
the-prisoner.line: A well known Napa red blend built on Zinfandel, ripe and bold.
the-prisoner.tell: The Prisoner is a famous Napa red blend led by Zinfandel with other dark grapes. It is ripe, bold and jammy, with spice and vanilla. Guests often ask for it; good with richer meats.

cesarini-sforza.name: Cesarini Sforza
cesarini-sforza.line: A Trentino sparkling house making Trento DOC wine by the Champagne method in the mountains.
cesarini-sforza.tell: Cesarini Sforza makes sparkling wine in Trento, in the Alps, the same way Champagne is made. The rosé brut is crisp, dry and lightly red fruited. A smart, good value alternative to Champagne for a toast.

nicchia.name: Nicchia (Cantina Carafoli)
nicchia.line: A Lambrusco di Modena from the Carafoli family, a long established winery near Modena.
nicchia.tell: Nicchia is made by the Carafoli family near Modena. Lambrusco is a lightly sparkling red, fresh and fruity, and this one blends several Lambrusco grapes. Serve it chilled; it is lovely with rich, salty food and a happy surprise for guests who think red wine cannot sparkle.

demarie.name: Demarie
demarie.line: A family estate in the Roero hills of Piedmont, across the river from the Langhe, making Arneis and Nebbiolo.
demarie.tell: Demarie is a family winery in the Roero, sandy hills north of Alba. Arneis is the local white grape: dry, soft and lightly floral, with pear and almond. An easy, good value white for shellfish or salads.

frecciarossa.name: Frecciarossa
frecciarossa.line: A long established estate in the Oltrepò Pavese hills of southern Lombardy.
frecciarossa.tell: Frecciarossa is a family estate in the Oltrepò Pavese, hills south of Milan. Its Pinot Grigio is fresh and clean, with a little more texture than the everyday kind. A safe, friendly white for fish or salads.

massolino.name: Massolino
massolino.line: A family estate in Serralunga d'Alba, known for firm, fine Barolo, above all from the Vigna Rionda vineyard.
massolino.tell: Massolino is a family winery in Serralunga, the village known for the most structured Barolo. Vigna Rionda is their most famous site: deep, firm and long lived, and the list holds Riserva and magnums. The Barbera, Barbaresco and Riesling are friendlier entries.

colleleva.name: Colleleva
colleleva.line: A small estate in the hills of the Marche near the Adriatic, making fresh, good value wines from local grapes.
colleleva.tell: Colleleva is a small estate in the Marche, between the Apennines and the Adriatic. The Rosso Piceno is mostly Montepulciano with some Sangiovese: juicy, red fruited and easy, made in steel to keep it fresh. A great value red for pasta or a casual meal.

elvio-cogno.name: Elvio Cogno
elvio-cogno.line: A family estate in Novello, in the Barolo zone, known for elegant Barolo from the Ravera vineyard.
elvio-cogno.tell: Elvio Cogno is a family estate in Novello, at the south west of the Barolo zone. Ravera is their top Barolo: fine, perfumed and firm. Montegrilli is a Langhe Nebbiolo, younger and friendlier, a gentle introduction to the grape at a fair price.

ronchi.name: Azienda Agricola Ronchi
ronchi.line: A small family estate in the Barbaresco zone.
ronchi.tell: Ronchi is a small family estate in Barbaresco. Barbaresco is Nebbiolo, perfumed and firm, with red cherry, rose and fine tannin. This half bottle is a good way for two guests to try it.

ca-marcanda.name: Ca' Marcanda (Gaja)
ca-marcanda.line: The Gaja family's estate on the Tuscan coast near Bolgheri, making Bordeaux style reds.
ca-marcanda.tell: Ca' Marcanda is the Gaja family's estate near Bolgheri, on the Tuscan coast. The reds use Bordeaux grapes. Promis is the friendly entry, Magari the middle wine, and Camarcanda the top: polished and deep. Magari comes in half bottle too.

gaja.name: Gaja
gaja.line: The most famous name in Barbaresco, known for its Barbaresco and single vineyards such as Sorì San Lorenzo, Sorì Tildìn and Costa Russi.
gaja.tell: Gaja put Barbaresco on the world map. The Barbaresco is fine and perfumed; Sorì San Lorenzo, Sorì Tildìn and Costa Russi are single vineyards sold as Langhe, and Darmagi is a rare Piedmont Cabernet. Celebration bottles. The family also owns Pieve Santa Restituta, Ca' Marcanda and IDDA.

la-spinetta.name: La Spinetta
la-spinetta.line: A family estate known for ripe, modern Barbaresco from single vineyards.
la-spinetta.tell: La Spinetta is the Rivetti family estate, known for a rich, modern style. Bordini and Valeirano are Barbaresco vineyards: dark fruited and polished, more generous than traditional Barbaresco. Bordini comes in half bottle.

dal-forno.name: Dal Forno Romano
dal-forno.line: A cult estate east of Verona making extremely concentrated Amarone and Valpolicella.
dal-forno.tell: Dal Forno makes some of the most powerful wines in Italy, in the Val d'Illasi east of Verona. Even the Valpolicella is dense and dark; the Amarone, from dried grapes, is huge, sweet fruited and long. A rare bottle for a guest who loves big wine; decant.

foradori.name: Foradori
foradori.line: A biodynamic Trentino estate, led by Elisabetta Foradori, that revived the local Teroldego grape.
foradori.tell: Foradori is the great name for Teroldego, a dark grape of the Trentino mountains. Sgarzon is aged in clay amphorae: fresh, juicy and lightly earthy, with dark berries. A fun magnum for a table that likes lighter, natural style reds.

fuligni.name: Fuligni
fuligni.line: A family estate in Montalcino making elegant, traditional Brunello.
fuligni.tell: Fuligni is a family estate just east of Montalcino. Its Brunello is fine and fragrant rather than heavy, with cherry, leather and herbs. The Riserva in magnum is a grand choice for a table eating beef.

quintarelli.name: Giuseppe Quintarelli
quintarelli.line: The legendary traditional producer of Valpolicella, famous for Amarone and wines aged for years before release.
quintarelli.tell: Quintarelli is the legend of Valpolicella. The Amarone is deep and layered; Rosso del Bepi is made in years when Amarone is not; Alzero uses dried Cabernet grapes; Ca' del Merlo is a ripasso style red. Amabile del Cere and Recioto are sweet. Rare bottles; decant the reds.

l-arco.name: L'Arco
l-arco.line: A small Valpolicella estate run by Luca Fedrigo, who learned from Giuseppe Quintarelli.
l-arco.tell: L'Arco is a small estate run by Luca Fedrigo, who worked for years with Quintarelli. Pario is a rich, layered Valpolicella; the Verona Rosso is lighter. A smart way into Quintarelli's style at a gentler price.

le-ragnaie.name: Le Ragnaie
le-ragnaie.line: A Montalcino estate with some of the highest vineyards in the zone, making fresh, fragrant Brunello.
le-ragnaie.tell: Le Ragnaie farms very high vineyards in Montalcino, so its Brunello is fresh and fragrant, with red fruit and fine tannin. Casanovina Montosoli is a single vineyard bottling. A great Brunello for a guest who likes elegance.

luigi-giordano.name: Luigi Giordano
luigi-giordano.line: A family estate in Barbaresco making traditional wines, including from the Montestefano vineyard.
luigi-giordano.tell: Luigi Giordano is a family estate in the village of Barbaresco. Montestefano is one of the village's most powerful vineyards: dark, firm and long lived Nebbiolo. Here in magnum for a table to share.

antinori.name: Marchesi Antinori
antinori.line: One of Italy's oldest wine families, whose Tignanello and Solaia helped create the Super Tuscan style.
antinori.tell: Antinori is one of the great Florentine wine families. Tignanello, Sangiovese with Cabernet, was one of the first Super Tuscans; Solaia, mostly Cabernet, is the grander one. Both are rich, polished and long lived. Guests often know the names.

oddero.name: Oddero
oddero.line: A historic family estate in La Morra with holdings in many of the great Barolo and Barbaresco vineyards.
oddero.tell: Oddero is an old family estate with vines in many famous crus. Brunate and Rocche di Castiglione are perfumed, Bussia Vigna Mondoca and Villero deeper, and Vignarionda firm and grand. Gallina is their Barbaresco. Classic, traditional Nebbiolo, with many magnums on the list.

pieve-santa-restituta.name: Pieve Santa Restituta (Gaja)
pieve-santa-restituta.line: The Gaja family's estate in Montalcino, making Brunello including the single vineyards Rennina and Sugarille.
pieve-santa-restituta.tell: Pieve Santa Restituta is the Gaja family estate in Montalcino. The Brunello is polished and deep. Rennina is the more fragrant single vineyard and Sugarille the firmer one. A strong name for a guest who loves Gaja or wants a celebration Brunello.

poggio-di-sotto.name: Poggio di Sotto
poggio-di-sotto.line: A Montalcino estate near Castelnuovo dell'Abate, admired for pale, fragrant, traditional Brunello.
poggio-di-sotto.tell: Poggio di Sotto makes some of the most graceful Brunello, from slopes in the south of Montalcino. It is fragrant and fine, with red fruit and spice, and ages superbly. Rare; the Riserva and magnum are celebration bottles.

sesti.name: Sesti
sesti.line: A small Montalcino estate known for elegant, traditional Brunello.
sesti.tell: Sesti is a small family estate in the south of Montalcino. The Brunello is elegant and savoury, made in a traditional way. A lovely choice with beef or lamb; the magnum suits a larger table.

montenidoli.name: Montenidoli
montenidoli.line: A San Gimignano estate run by Elisabetta Fagiuoli, making characterful whites and reds from Tuscan grapes.
montenidoli.tell: Montenidoli is a family estate in San Gimignano, better known for white. Triassico is a red, named for the ancient soils: fresh, savoury and fragrant. The list holds it in magnum across vintages, a good pick for a table sharing pasta or poultry.

conestabile-della-staffe.name: Conestabile della Staffe
conestabile-della-staffe.line: A small Umbrian estate making natural wines from local grapes.
conestabile-della-staffe.tell: Conestabile della Staffe is a small natural wine estate in Umbria. Ciliegio is made from Ciliegiolo, a local grape whose name means cherry: light, juicy and lively. A fun red for an adventurous guest, lovely slightly cool.

masseria-del-pino.name: Masseria del Pino
masseria-del-pino.line: A small organic and biodynamic farm on Mount Etna, making wine by hand from very old vines.
masseria-del-pino.tell: Masseria del Pino is a tiny farm on Etna that makes wine by hand from very old vines. I Nove Fratelli is mostly Nerello Mascalese: fragrant, savoury and mineral, with cherry and herbs. A great pick for a guest who loves Burgundy or Barolo.

radikon.name: Radikon
radikon.line: A family estate on the Slovenian border in Friuli, pioneers of long skin contact wines.
radikon.tell: Radikon is a family estate near the Slovenian border, famous for its orange wines. The reds are made with the same patience: long aged and savoury. They use 500 ml bottles. An adventurous choice; ask the sommelier how they are drinking.

vigneti-vecchio.name: Vigneti Vecchio
vigneti-vecchio.line: A small Etna estate working very old vines on the north slope of the volcano.
vigneti-vecchio.tell: Vigneti Vecchio is a small Etna family estate working old vines in volcanic sand. Sciare Vive is mostly Nerello Mascalese with a little of other local grapes: medium bodied, silky and peppery. A fresh, savoury red for poultry or pork.

grosjean.name: Grosjean
grosjean.line: A family estate in the alpine Valle d'Aosta, making fresh mountain wines.
grosjean.tell: Grosjean is a family estate in the Valle d'Aosta, high in the Alps. Their Gamay is light, bright and red fruited, like a mountain Beaujolais. A gentle red for fish or poultry, best a little cool.

bruno-giacosa.name: Bruno Giacosa
bruno-giacosa.line: One of the great traditional names of Barbaresco and Barolo; Asili is among its most celebrated Barbarescos.
bruno-giacosa.tell: Bruno Giacosa is one of the legends of Piedmont. Asili is a famous Barbaresco vineyard: fragrant, fine and long lived. A celebration bottle for a Nebbiolo lover; decant.

produttori-del-barbaresco.name: Produttori del Barbaresco
produttori-del-barbaresco.line: The village cooperative of Barbaresco, admired for traditional wines and single vineyard Riservas.
produttori-del-barbaresco.tell: Produttori del Barbaresco is the village cooperative, and one of the best in Italy. The Barbaresco is classic and fair priced. Asili, Montefico, Ovello and Rabajà are single vineyards, each with its own character. Great value for Nebbiolo lovers.

ca-rome.name: Ca' Rome'
ca-rome.line: A family estate in Barbaresco making traditional Barbaresco and Barolo.
ca-rome.tell: Ca' Rome' is a family estate in Barbaresco. Rio Sordo and Chiaramanti are Barbaresco vineyards, perfumed and firm; Rapet is a Barolo from Serralunga, deeper and sterner. Classic Nebbiolo for beef or game.

cocito.name: Cocito
cocito.line: A small family estate in the Barbaresco zone.
cocito.tell: Cocito is a small family producer in Barbaresco. Baluchin Riserva is aged longer before release: perfumed Nebbiolo with red fruit, rose and firm tannin. Ask the sommelier how the vintage is drinking.

roagna.name: Roagna (I Paglieri)
roagna.line: A deeply traditional family estate in Barbaresco, making long aged wines from old vines.
roagna.tell: Roagna is one of the most traditional estates in Piedmont, with long fermentations and long ageing. Pajè, Crichët Pajé, Asili, Albesani, Faset and Gallina are Barbaresco vineyards; La Pira is Barolo. Fine, fragrant and long lived; decant.

scarpa.name: Scarpa
scarpa.line: A traditional Piedmont house known for holding its wines back for years before release.
scarpa.tell: Scarpa is a traditional house in Piedmont that often releases wines with age. Podere Barberis is their Barbaresco: fragrant and savoury, with mature notes. Ask the sommelier how the vintage is drinking.

vietti.name: Vietti
vietti.line: A leading Barolo estate in Castiglione Falletto, bottling famous single vineyards.
vietti.tell: Vietti is one of Barolo's best known estates. Ravera, Lazzarito and Cerequio are single vineyards: Ravera fresh and floral, Lazzarito firm, Cerequio silky. Masseria is a Barbaresco. Classic, polished Nebbiolo.

bartolo-mascarello.name: Bartolo Mascarello
bartolo-mascarello.line: A revered traditional estate in the village of Barolo that blends several vineyards into one wine.
bartolo-mascarello.tell: Bartolo Mascarello makes one Barolo, blended from several vineyards, the old way. It is fragrant, firm and very long lived, and collectors treasure it. The list holds many vintages; ask the sommelier which is ready and decant.

cappellano.name: Cappellano
cappellano.line: A small, very traditional Serralunga estate with a devoted following; Pie Rupestris is one of its Barolos.
cappellano.tell: Cappellano is a tiny traditional estate in Serralunga. Otin Fiorin Pie Rupestris is a Barolo from their old vineyard: fragrant, firm and savoury. Rare; ask the sommelier about it.

conterno-fantino.name: Conterno Fantino
conterno-fantino.line: A Monforte d'Alba estate making polished, modern minded Barolo.
conterno-fantino.tell: Conterno Fantino is a family estate in Monforte d'Alba. Mosconi Vigna Ped is a single vineyard Barolo: rich, dark and firm. A good Barolo for steak or braised meat.

fontanafredda.name: Fontanafredda
fontanafredda.line: A historic Serralunga estate founded on land once owned by Italy's first king.
fontanafredda.tell: Fontanafredda is a historic estate in Serralunga, linked to Italy's first king. La Rosa, La Villa and Lazzarito are single vineyard Barolos, and the Riserva is aged longer. Firm, classic Nebbiolo for beef and game.

brovia.name: Brovia
brovia.line: A traditional family estate in Castiglione Falletto, making classic Barolo.
brovia.tell: Brovia is a family estate in Castiglione Falletto, making Barolo the traditional way: fragrant, firm and long lived. A classic choice for a Nebbiolo lover.

gd-vajra.name: G.D. Vajra
gd-vajra.line: A family estate in the high hamlet of Vergne, making fresh, fragrant Barolo.
gd-vajra.tell: Vajra farms high vineyards near the village of Barolo, so its wines are fresh and perfumed. Albe is its Barolo blended from several high sites: bright, floral and approachable for Barolo. A smart entry to the region.

borgogno.name: Borgogno
borgogno.line: One of the oldest houses in the village of Barolo, known for long aged Riservas.
borgogno.tell: Borgogno is a historic house in the village of Barolo. The Riserva is aged longer before release and is classic, savoury and long. Ask the sommelier about the vintage before you recommend it.

giovanni-viberti.name: Giovanni Viberti
giovanni-viberti.line: A family estate in the Barolo zone making traditional Riserva Barolo.
giovanni-viberti.tell: Viberti is a family estate near the village of Barolo. Bricco delle Viole and San Pietro are Riserva Barolos: fragrant, savoury and firm. Good with beef, lamb or game.

giuseppe-mascarello.name: Giuseppe Mascarello e Figlio
giuseppe-mascarello.line: A great traditional family estate whose Monprivato Barolo is one of the most admired in Piedmont.
giuseppe-mascarello.tell: Giuseppe Mascarello is one of the great traditional names of Barolo. Monprivato is their famous vineyard in Castiglione Falletto: fragrant, fine and long lived. They also make a lovely Dolcetto from Santo Stefano di Perno. Rare; decant the Barolo.

piero-benevelli.name: Piero Benevelli
piero-benevelli.line: A small family estate in Monforte d'Alba.
piero-benevelli.tell: Piero Benevelli is a small family producer in Monforte d'Alba. Mosconi is a Barolo vineyard known for depth and structure. Ask the sommelier about its style and readiness.

fantino.name: Alessandro e Gian Natale Fantino
fantino.line: A small family estate in Monforte d'Alba making traditional Nebbiolo.
fantino.tell: Fantino is a small family estate in Monforte d'Alba. Rosso dei Dardi is a Nebbiolo from their vineyard: fragrant and savoury, with firm tannin. A thoughtful, fair priced Piedmont red.

ar-pe-pe.name: Ar.Pe.Pe.
ar-pe-pe.line: A family estate in alpine Valtellina making fine, long lived Nebbiolo from steep terraces.
ar-pe-pe.tell: Ar.Pe.Pe. farms steep terraces in Valtellina, in the Alps near Switzerland, where Nebbiolo is called Chiavennasca. The wines are lighter and more delicate than Barolo: fragrant, fresh and fine. Sassella, Grumello and Inferno are named sites. A great pick for a Burgundy lover.

castello-conti.name: Castello Conti
castello-conti.line: A small family estate in the hills of northern Piedmont making fragrant Nebbiolo based wines.
castello-conti.tell: Castello Conti is a small family estate in northern Piedmont, near the Alps. Il Rosso delle Donne is from Boca, Nebbiolo with local grapes: fragrant, fresh and mineral. A lighter cousin of Barolo.

luigi-ferrando.name: Luigi Ferrando
luigi-ferrando.line: The leading family of Carema, an alpine Nebbiolo zone on stone terraces near the Valle d'Aosta.
luigi-ferrando.tell: Ferrando is the name in Carema, tiny alpine terraces at the edge of Piedmont. Etichetta Nera, the black label, is their top selection: fragrant, fine and long lived Nebbiolo, lighter than Barolo. A treasure for a Nebbiolo lover.

monsecco.name: Monsecco
monsecco.line: An estate in Ghemme in northern Piedmont, making Nebbiolo based wines.
monsecco.tell: Monsecco makes Ghemme, a Nebbiolo zone in northern Piedmont. Expect a fragrant, firm red, lighter than Barolo, with red fruit and earth. Good with mushrooms, game or roast meats.

muraje.name: Muraje
muraje.line: A small producer in Carema, the alpine Nebbiolo zone of stone terraces.
muraje.tell: Muraje is a small producer in Carema, where Nebbiolo grows on stone terraces in the foothills of the Alps. Sumié is fragrant and fresh, with fine tannin. Ask the sommelier about this rare bottle.

silvio-giamello.name: Silvio Giamello
silvio-giamello.line: A small family producer in the Langhe hills of Piedmont.
silvio-giamello.tell: Silvio Giamello is a small family producer in the Langhe. Villa Gentiana is a Langhe red; ask the sommelier about the grape and style before you describe it.

travaglini.name: Travaglini
travaglini.line: The leading estate of Gattinara in northern Piedmont, recognisable by its curved bottle.
travaglini.tell: Travaglini is the best known name in Gattinara, northern Piedmont, and its bottle has a curved shape guests remember. The Riserva is Nebbiolo: fragrant, savoury and firm, with age. A good value Nebbiolo for beef or game.

elena-walch.name: Elena Walch
elena-walch.line: A leading family estate in Alto Adige, known for fresh, precise whites and Pinot Nero.
elena-walch.tell: Elena Walch is a family estate in Alto Adige, the Italian Alps. Ludwig is their top Pinot Nero: fresh, fine and red fruited, with good depth. An elegant red for salmon, duck or veal.

ferruccio-carlotto.name: Ferruccio Carlotto
ferruccio-carlotto.line: A small Alto Adige family estate known for Pinot Nero from Mazzon.
ferruccio-carlotto.tell: Carlotto is a small family estate in Alto Adige. Mazzon is a famous slope for Pinot Nero, and Filari di Mazzon is fragrant and fine, with red fruit and spice. A lovely, lighter red for fish or poultry.

miani.name: Miani
miani.line: A tiny, revered Friuli estate making very low yield, concentrated wines.
miani.tell: Miani is a tiny Friuli estate with a cult following, known for very low yields. Filip is a Merlot: deep, concentrated and polished. Rare; ask the sommelier about the vintage.

cantina-terlano.name: Cantina Terlano
cantina-terlano.line: An Alto Adige cooperative famous for long lived wines, here a Pinot Noir.
cantina-terlano.tell: Terlano is a celebrated cooperative in Alto Adige, best known for whites that age for decades. Monticol is its Pinot Noir: fine, fresh and red fruited. An elegant choice for salmon, veal or duck.

bertani.name: Bertani
bertani.line: A historic Verona house known for traditional, long aged Amarone.
bertani.tell: Bertani is a historic name in Valpolicella. Its Amarone Classico is made traditionally from dried grapes and aged long: rich, dried cherry and spice, but dry. A classic choice for braised meats or hard cheese.

marchesi-biscardo.name: Marchesi Biscardo
marchesi-biscardo.line: A Veneto producer making an approachable Corvina based red from near Verona.
