marchesi-biscardo.tell: Marchesi Biscardo makes a Verona red from Corvina, the main grape of Valpolicella. It is round and fruity, with cherry and plum. An easy, good value red for pasta or chicken.

masi.name: Masi
masi.line: A leading Valpolicella house and a specialist in wines from dried grapes, including several Amarones.
masi.tell: Masi is one of the great names of Amarone, made from grapes dried for months. Costasera is the classic, rich and velvety; Campolongo di Torbe and Mazzano are single vineyards, deeper and longer. Big wines for braised meats and cheese.

castello-di-ama.name: Castello di Ama
castello-di-ama.line: A leading Chianti Classico estate in Gaiole, known for fine Sangiovese and contemporary art.
castello-di-ama.tell: Castello di Ama is a top Chianti Classico estate, also famous for the art installed around its hamlet. San Lorenzo is its Gran Selezione: fine, firm Sangiovese. Haiku is a blend. Elegant Tuscan reds for beef or veal.

cecchi.name: Cecchi
cecchi.line: A long established Tuscan family house making reliable Chianti.
cecchi.tell: Cecchi is a family wine house in Tuscany. Its Chianti is fresh and easy, with cherry and a savoury finish. A friendly value red for pasta or poultry.

collazzi.name: Collazzi
collazzi.line: An estate in the hills south of Florence making Chianti Classico and Tuscan reds.
collazzi.tell: Collazzi is an estate in the hills just south of Florence. Bastioni is its Chianti Classico: fresh Sangiovese with cherry and herbs. A good value Tuscan red for pasta or veal.

felsina.name: Fattoria di Fèlsina
felsina.line: A Chianti Classico estate in Castelnuovo Berardenga, known for Rancia and for pure Sangiovese.
felsina.tell: Fèlsina is a top estate at the southern edge of Chianti Classico. Rancia Riserva is one of the region's classic single vineyard Sangioveses: firm and long. Maestro Raro is their Cabernet. Great Tuscan reds for beef.

mazzei.name: Mazzei (Castello di Fonterutoli)
mazzei.line: An old Tuscan family whose Castello di Fonterutoli estate makes Chianti Classico and the Siepi blend.
mazzei.tell: The Mazzei family has made wine in Tuscany for centuries. Fonterutoli is their Chianti Classico, fresh and classic; Siepi is a richer blend of Sangiovese and Merlot. Philip is another of their reds. Reliable, polished Tuscan wines.

la-sala.name: La Sala
la-sala.line: A Chianti Classico estate whose Il Torriano is a Gran Selezione, the top tier of the region.
la-sala.tell: La Sala is a Chianti Classico estate. Il Torriano is a Gran Selezione, the region's top category: structured Sangiovese with dark cherry and spice. Good with beef or lamb.

tolaini.name: Tolaini
tolaini.line: An estate at the southern end of Chianti Classico making Gran Selezione and the Picconero blend.
tolaini.tell: Tolaini is an estate in the south of Chianti Classico. The Gran Selezione is firm, polished Sangiovese, and Picconero is a richer Bordeaux style blend. Both suit beef and lamb.

villa-di-geggiano.name: Villa di Geggiano
villa-di-geggiano.line: A historic villa estate near Siena making traditional Chianti Classico.
villa-di-geggiano.tell: Villa di Geggiano is an old family villa near Siena. The Chianti Classico Riserva is traditional: savoury Sangiovese with cherry, leather and herbs. Several vintages and a magnum are on the list.

croce-di-febo.name: Croce di Febo
croce-di-febo.line: A small estate making Vino Nobile di Montepulciano.
croce-di-febo.tell: Croce di Febo makes Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, a Sangiovese from the hill town of Montepulciano in Tuscany, not the Montepulciano grape. Expect cherry, earth and firm tannin. A fair priced Tuscan red.

altesino.name: Altesino
altesino.line: A Montalcino estate known for its Brunello from the famous Montosoli hill.
altesino.tell: Altesino is a well known Montalcino estate. Its Brunello is classic and balanced; Montosoli is a famous hill north of town, giving a finer, more perfumed Brunello. Great with beef.

caparzo.name: Caparzo
caparzo.line: A Montalcino estate whose La Casa is a single vineyard Brunello.
caparzo.tell: Caparzo is a Montalcino estate. La Casa is its single vineyard Brunello: deep, firm Sangiovese with cherry and spice. A solid, classic choice with steak.

casanova-di-neri.name: Casanova di Neri
casanova-di-neri.line: A Montalcino estate known for rich, modern Brunello; Tenuta Nuova is its best known wine.
casanova-di-neri.tell: Casanova di Neri makes Brunello in a rich, modern style. Tenuta Nuova is its most famous wine: dark, ripe and polished. A good Brunello for a guest who likes fuller reds.

cerbaiona.name: Cerbaiona
cerbaiona.line: A small, celebrated Montalcino estate making refined, traditional Brunello.
cerbaiona.tell: Cerbaiona is a small, much admired estate in Montalcino. Its Brunello is fine, fragrant and long lived. A treat for a Brunello lover; decant.

col-d-orcia.name: Col d'Orcia
col-d-orcia.line: A large, historic Montalcino estate, farmed organically; Poggio al Vento is its Riserva.
col-d-orcia.tell: Col d'Orcia is one of the largest estates in Montalcino. Poggio al Vento is its single vineyard Riserva, aged longer: deep, savoury and long. A classic Brunello for beef or game.

cinelli-colombini.name: Donatella Cinelli Colombini
cinelli-colombini.line: A Montalcino estate run by Donatella Cinelli Colombini, known for its team of women winemakers.
cinelli-colombini.tell: Donatella Cinelli Colombini runs a Montalcino estate with an all women team. Prime Donne is a Brunello: elegant and fragrant. They also make a sweet Vin Santo, here in half bottle for dessert.

il-marroneto.name: Il Marroneto
il-marroneto.line: A small Montalcino estate admired for pale, perfumed, traditional Brunello.
il-marroneto.tell: Il Marroneto is a small estate just outside the town of Montalcino. Its Brunello is fragrant and fine rather than heavy; Madonna delle Grazie is the celebrated single vineyard. A great pick for a guest who loves elegance.

il-poggione.name: Il Poggione
il-poggione.line: A historic family estate in the south of Montalcino making classic Brunello.
il-poggione.tell: Il Poggione is a historic family estate in southern Montalcino. Its Brunello is classic and generous, with cherry, leather and spice. A reliable choice for steak.

podere-santa-maria.name: Podere Santa Maria (Colleoni)
podere-santa-maria.line: A tiny biodynamic Montalcino estate run by the Colleoni family, making elegant, traditional Brunello.
podere-santa-maria.tell: Podere Santa Maria is a tiny biodynamic estate run by Marino and Luisa Colleoni. The Brunello is fine and fragrant, aged in large casks. Poggio Sant'Arna is a rare single parcel Riserva. Ask the sommelier about these small production bottles.

biondi-santi.name: Biondi-Santi (Tenuta Greppo)
biondi-santi.line: The family estate credited with creating Brunello di Montalcino, famous for long lived Riservas.
biondi-santi.tell: Biondi-Santi is the family that created Brunello at Tenuta Greppo. The wines are fresh, firm and built for decades: the Annata is the standard Brunello, the Riserva the long lived flagship, and the Rosso the younger wine. Historic bottles; decant.

val-di-suga.name: Val di Suga
val-di-suga.line: A Montalcino estate with vineyards in different parts of the zone; Vigna del Lago is a single vineyard Brunello.
val-di-suga.tell: Val di Suga makes Brunello from several corners of Montalcino. Vigna del Lago is a single vineyard bottling: deeper and more structured than the standard. Good with beef.

arcanum.name: Arcanum
arcanum.line: A Tuscan estate near Castelnuovo Berardenga making Bordeaux style reds.
arcanum.tell: Arcanum is a Tuscan estate making Bordeaux style reds in the south of Chianti country. The Toscana Rosso is rich and polished, with dark fruit. A good choice for a guest who loves Napa or Bordeaux.

banfi.name: Banfi
banfi.line: A large Montalcino estate making Brunello, Super Tuscan blends and a sweet Moscadello.
banfi.tell: Banfi is one of the largest estates in Montalcino. Summus is a rich red blend, Stilnovo another Tuscan red, and Florus is a sweet late harvest Moscadello di Montalcino for dessert.

bibi-graetz.name: Bibi Graetz
bibi-graetz.line: A Tuscan winemaker and artist, known for Testamatta, a vivid Sangiovese.
bibi-graetz.tell: Bibi Graetz is an artist and winemaker based near Florence. Testamatta, meaning crazy head, is his top Sangiovese: bright, fragrant and intense. A modern Tuscan red for beef or veal.

masseto.name: Masseto
masseto.line: The famous Bolgheri Merlot, born at Tenuta dell'Ornellaia, one of Italy's most celebrated and costly wines.
masseto.tell: Masseto is a Merlot from a clay hill in Bolgheri, born at Ornellaia. It is deep, velvety and long lived, one of the most famous wines in Italy. Trophy bottles; involve the sommelier and decant.

prelius.name: Prelius (Castelprile)
prelius.line: The organic Maremma estate of the family behind Castello di Volpaia, near the Tuscan coast.
prelius.tell: Prelius is the Maremma estate of the family who own Castello di Volpaia in Chianti, a few miles from the sea. Castelprile Riserva blends Sangiovese with Bordeaux grapes: ripe, smooth and dark fruited. Good with beef or lamb.

biserno.name: Tenuta di Biserno
biserno.line: A coastal Tuscan estate founded by Lodovico and Piero Antinori, making Bordeaux style reds.
biserno.tell: Biserno is a coastal Tuscan estate of Lodovico Antinori, who founded Ornellaia, and his brother Piero. Il Pino di Biserno is the second wine; Biserno the grand one. Rich, polished Bordeaux style reds.

tenuta-san-guido.name: Tenuta San Guido
tenuta-san-guido.line: The Bolgheri estate that created Sassicaia, the first famous Italian Cabernet; Guidalberto is its younger red.
tenuta-san-guido.tell: Tenuta San Guido made Sassicaia, the wine that began the Super Tuscans and has its own appellation. It is Cabernet led: elegant, fresh and long lived. Guidalberto is the younger, friendlier red. Guests know the name.

sette-cieli.name: Tenuta Sette Cieli
sette-cieli.line: A hillside estate above Bolgheri making Bordeaux style reds.
sette-cieli.tell: Sette Cieli, meaning seven skies, farms high vineyards above the Bolgheri coast. Indaco, Scipio and Yantra are its reds from Bordeaux grapes: fresh, polished and fine. Ask the sommelier which grape leads each.

arnaldo-caprai.name: Arnaldo Caprai
arnaldo-caprai.line: The estate that championed Sagrantino di Montefalco, a dark, very tannic Umbrian red.
arnaldo-caprai.tell: Caprai did more than anyone to make Sagrantino known. It is one of the most tannic reds in the world: dark, powerful and long. The 25 Anni bottling is the flagship. Decant, and pair with braised meat or game.

paolo-bea.name: Paolo Bea
paolo-bea.line: A traditional, natural minded family estate in Montefalco, Umbria.
paolo-bea.tell: Paolo Bea makes wine the old way in Montefalco. Pagliaro is a powerful Sagrantino, and Rosso de Veo is a blend. Wild, savoury and deep. An adventurous choice; decant.

emidio-pepe.name: Emidio Pepe
emidio-pepe.line: A legendary Abruzzo family estate making Montepulciano by hand and releasing older vintages from its cellar.
emidio-pepe.tell: Emidio Pepe makes Montepulciano d'Abruzzo the traditional way and holds bottles back for years. The wines are earthy, deep and long lived. The list holds several vintages; ask the sommelier which is ready and decant carefully.

luigi-tecce.name: Luigi Tecce
luigi-tecce.line: A small Campania grower making powerful, natural minded Aglianico.
luigi-tecce.tell: Luigi Tecce makes Aglianico in the hills of Irpinia, Campania. Poliphemo and Puro Sangue are Taurasi: dark, smoky and firm. Satyricon is a little lighter. Big wines for lamb or beef.

mastroberardino.name: Mastroberardino
mastroberardino.line: The historic family of Campania wine, guardians of Aglianico and Taurasi.
mastroberardino.tell: Mastroberardino is the great old name of Campania. Radici Taurasi is Aglianico: dark, firm and long lived, sometimes called the Barolo of the south. Good with braised meats.

benanti.name: Benanti
benanti.line: A pioneering family estate of the modern Etna revival.
benanti.tell: Benanti helped start the modern revival of Mount Etna. Their Etna Rosso is Nerello Mascalese: fragrant, light bodied and mineral, often compared to Pinot Noir. A great choice with tuna, pork or poultry.

cos.name: COS
cos.line: A Sicilian estate known for natural winemaking and Cerasuolo di Vittoria.
cos.tell: COS is a natural minded estate in south east Sicily. Cerasuolo di Vittoria blends Nero d'Avola with Frappato: bright, juicy and floral. Lovely slightly cool with fish or poultry.

frank-cornelissen.name: Frank Cornelissen
frank-cornelissen.line: A Belgian born winemaker on Etna, known for natural wines and single contrada Munjebel reds.
frank-cornelissen.tell: Frank Cornelissen makes natural wine on Etna. His Munjebel reds come from single contrade, the local name for vineyards, each a little different: fragrant, savoury and mineral. An adventurous pick for a curious guest.

idda.name: IDDA
idda.line: A partnership between Angelo Gaja and Sicilian grower Alberto Graci on Mount Etna.
idda.tell: IDDA is Angelo Gaja's project on Etna with local grower Alberto Graci. The Etna Rosso is fragrant and fine, with red fruit and volcanic minerality. A good story for a guest who knows Gaja.

i-vigneri.name: I Vigneri di Salvo Foti
i-vigneri.line: Salvo Foti's group of Etna growers, working old vines by hand in the traditional way.
i-vigneri.tell: Salvo Foti is one of Etna's most respected viticulturists, and I Vigneri works old vines by traditional methods. Vinupetra is a deep, mineral Etna Rosso. A wine with real character.

palari.name: Palari
palari.line: A small estate near Messina known for reviving Faro, a fragrant Sicilian red.
palari.tell: Palari is a small estate in the hills near Messina. Rosso del Soprano is a red from local grapes: fragrant, fine and savoury. A lovely, unusual Sicilian red.

passopisciaro.name: Passopisciaro
passopisciaro.line: An Etna estate founded by Andrea Franchetti that bottles single contrade.
passopisciaro.tell: Passopisciaro was one of the first Etna estates to bottle single contrade. Guardiola and Sciaranuova are separate high sites: fragrant, mineral Nerello Mascalese. Elegant reds for poultry or pork.

terre-nere.name: Tenuta delle Terre Nere
terre-nere.line: A leading Etna estate known for single contrada reds, including a wine from ungrafted old vines.
terre-nere.tell: Terre Nere is a top Etna estate. Calderara Sottana and Moganazzi are single contrade; Prephylloxera comes from very old vines that predate phylloxera. Fragrant, mineral reds often compared to Burgundy.

borgo-scopeto.name: Borgo Scopeto
borgo-scopeto.line: A Chianti Classico estate near Siena, in the same family as Caparzo and Altesino.
borgo-scopeto.tell: Borgo Scopeto is a Chianti Classico estate near Siena. Its Vin Santo is a sweet wine made from dried grapes and aged in small barrels: nutty, honeyed and warm. Here in half bottle, lovely with dessert.

castello-di-volpaia.name: Castello di Volpaia
castello-di-volpaia.line: A medieval hilltop village estate in Radda, one of the leading names of Chianti Classico.
castello-di-volpaia.tell: Volpaia is a hilltop village estate in Radda, high in Chianti Classico. Its Vin Santo is made from dried grapes and aged slowly: amber, nutty and sweet. A lovely half bottle with dessert.

maculan.name: Maculan
maculan.line: A Veneto family estate famous for Torcolato, a sweet wine from dried grapes.
maculan.tell: Maculan is a family estate in Breganze, Veneto. Torcolato is made from grapes dried after harvest: golden, honeyed and rich, with good acidity. A beautiful half bottle with dessert or cheese.

marco-de-bartoli.name: Marco De Bartoli
marco-de-bartoli.line: A Sicilian family estate famous for Marsala and for sweet passito from the island of Pantelleria.
marco-de-bartoli.tell: De Bartoli is a great Sicilian family name. Bukkuram is a passito from Pantelleria, made from sun dried Muscat grapes: apricot, honey and orange peel. Wonderful with dessert or blue cheese.

chapel-down.name: Chapel Down
chapel-down.line: One of England's best known sparkling wine producers, in Kent, making wine by the Champagne method.
chapel-down.tell: Chapel Down is a leading English sparkling wine house in Kent, where chalky soils and a cool climate echo Champagne. The rosé brut is crisp and red fruited. A fun, good value alternative to Champagne and a nice talking point.

chateau-les-clauzots.name: Château les Clauzots
chateau-les-clauzots.line: A family estate in the south of the Graves, making white Bordeaux from Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon.
chateau-les-clauzots.tell: Les Clauzots has been in the same family for generations in the Graves, south of Bordeaux. The white is Sauvignon Blanc with Sémillon, aged on its lees: citrus and peach, with a round, silky texture. Great value with fish and shellfish.

stephane-ogier.name: Stéphane Ogier
stephane-ogier.line: A Côte-Rôtie family estate making fine Syrah, with good value wines from the wider Rhône.
stephane-ogier.tell: Ogier is a respected Côte-Rôtie estate. Le Temps est Venu is its Côtes du Rhône, led by Grenache: warm red fruit, a little spice and soft tannin, at an easy price. A friendly red for poultry, pork or a mixed table.

chateau-massereau.name: Château Massereau
chateau-massereau.line: An organic family estate in Barsac that makes dry red Bordeaux Supérieur with minimal intervention.
chateau-massereau.tell: Massereau sits in Barsac, sweet wine country, but makes red too. Cuvée K blends Merlot and the Cabernets with Petit Verdot, farmed organically and made with little intervention: blackberry, tobacco and graphite, with some age. Remarkable value for mature Bordeaux.

chateau-ferriere.name: Château Ferrière
chateau-ferriere.line: A small third growth in Margaux making fragrant, elegant claret.
chateau-ferriere.tell: Ferrière is a small third growth in Margaux, the appellation known for perfume and finesse. Expect red and black fruit, violets and fine tannin. The half bottle is a lovely classed growth for two guests.

domaine-de-la-vougeraie.name: Domaine de la Vougeraie
domaine-de-la-vougeraie.line: The Boisset family estate, farmed biodynamically, with vines across the Côte d'Or, including the rare white Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot.
domaine-de-la-vougeraie.tell: Vougeraie is the Boisset family's Burgundy estate, farmed biodynamically. Le Clos Blanc is a rare thing: a white premier cru from Vougeot, a village known for red. Fine and mineral Chardonnay, here in magnum and double magnum for a celebration.

vincent-et-sophie-morey.name: Vincent et Sophie Morey
vincent-et-sophie-morey.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet family estate making clean, fresh whites and reds.
vincent-et-sophie-morey.tell: Vincent and Sophie Morey make wine in Chassagne-Montrachet. Les Embrazées is a Chassagne premier cru: fresh and generous, with citrus, white flowers and a touch of hazelnut. Here in magnum, a fine bottle for a table eating fish or crab.

guy-breton.name: Guy Breton
guy-breton.line: One of the original natural wine growers of Beaujolais, based in Morgon.
guy-breton.tell: Guy Breton was one of the growers who brought natural, carefully made Beaujolais back into fashion. His Fleurie is fragrant and silky, with red berries and flowers. Serve it slightly cool; the magnum is fun for a big table.

chateau-climens.name: Château Climens
chateau-climens.line: A first growth of Barsac, admired for sweet wines with unusual freshness and finesse.
chateau-climens.tell: Climens is a top estate in Barsac, next to Sauternes. Its sweet wine is famously fresh and fine: honey, citrus and apricot, with bright acidity. A beautiful match for fruit tarts, blue cheese or foie gras.

chateau-gilette.name: Château Gilette
chateau-gilette.line: A small Sauternes estate that ages its wines for many years in vat before release.
chateau-gilette.tell: Gilette is unique in Sauternes: it holds its wine for many years before bottling, so it arrives mature. Crème de Tête is the top selection: deep gold, with caramel, dried apricot and orange peel. A rare, lovely dessert wine.

chateau-suduiraut.name: Château Suduiraut
chateau-suduiraut.line: A first growth of Sauternes, next to Yquem, making rich, golden sweet wine.
chateau-suduiraut.tell: Suduiraut is a first growth in Sauternes, a neighbour of Yquem. The wine is rich and golden, with honey, apricot and pineapple. A generous choice with crème brûlée, fruit desserts or blue cheese; the half bottle suits two.

chateau-d-yquem.name: Château d'Yquem
chateau-d-yquem.line: The most famous sweet wine estate in the world, alone in its own top class in the Sauternes classification.
chateau-d-yquem.tell: Yquem is the most famous sweet wine in the world, given its own rank above every other Sauternes. It is rich, layered and extremely long lived, with honey, apricot and spice. The list has several vintages, half bottles and a magnum; involve the sommelier.

domaine-des-baumard.name: Domaine des Baumard
domaine-des-baumard.line: A family estate in Anjou making Chenin Blanc, dry and sweet.
domaine-des-baumard.tell: Baumard is a family estate in Anjou. Clos Sainte Catherine is a Coteaux du Layon: sweet Chenin Blanc, honeyed but fresh, with quince and apricot. Lovely with fruit desserts or cheese.

domaine-labet.name: Domaine Labet
domaine-labet.line: A family estate in the Jura, known for wines from distinct parcels.
domaine-labet.tell: Labet is a family estate in the Jura, in eastern France. Chercheurs d'Or sits with the dessert wines here, in half bottle. Ask the sommelier how sweet it is and how it is made before you describe it.

riveyrac.name: Riveyrac
riveyrac.line: A Roussillon name for long aged Rivesaltes, a fortified sweet wine of southern France.
riveyrac.tell: Riveyrac is known for Rivesaltes, a sweet fortified wine from Roussillon, near Spain, often aged for decades in wood. Expect dried fruit, nuts, caramel and spice. A great choice with chocolate or coffee desserts; ask about the vintage.

johanneshof-reinisch.name: Johanneshof Reinisch
johanneshof-reinisch.line: A family estate in Tattendorf, south of Vienna, known for Pinot Noir and the local red grapes.
johanneshof-reinisch.tell: The Reinisch family farms in Tattendorf, in the Thermenregion south of Vienna, a good spot for Pinot Noir. Ried Holzspur is a single vineyard Pinot: fresh, fine and red fruited. A smart alternative to Burgundy.

gut-oggau.name: Gut Oggau
gut-oggau.line: A biodynamic estate in Burgenland whose labels show imagined family members, one for each wine.
gut-oggau.tell: Gut Oggau farms biodynamically by Lake Neusiedl, and every label is a portrait of an imagined family member. Joschuari is Blaufränkisch: fresh, savoury and juicy, natural in style. A great talking point for an adventurous guest.

heinrich.name: Heinrich
heinrich.line: A biodynamic family estate in Gols, by Lake Neusiedl, making Blaufränkisch and other Austrian reds.
heinrich.tell: Heinrich is a biodynamic family estate in Gols, near Lake Neusiedl. Alter Berg is a Blaufränkisch from an old hillside site: dark cherry, pepper and firm freshness. A lovely red for duck, pork or game.

moric.name: Moric
moric.line: An estate that helped show how fine old vine Blaufränkisch from Burgenland can be.
moric.tell: Moric is one of the names that made Austrian Blaufränkisch famous. The Reserve is fresh and peppery, with dark berries and fine tannin, often compared to Northern Rhône or Burgundy. A thoughtful pick for a curious red drinker.

wiederstein.name: Winzerin Wiederstein
wiederstein.line: A small estate in Carnuntum, east of Vienna, making Blaufränkisch and other Austrian wines.
wiederstein.tell: Wiederstein is a small estate in Carnuntum, between Vienna and the Slovak border. Wei Damals is Blaufränkisch: fresh, juicy and peppery. A lighter red for poultry or pork.

lukas-hammelmann.name: Lukas Hammelmann
lukas-hammelmann.line: A young Pfalz grower making Pinot Noir and other wines in a fresh style.
lukas-hammelmann.tell: Lukas Hammelmann is a young grower in the Pfalz, in south west Germany, where Pinot Noir, called Spätburgunder, does well. Roter Berg and Dhochsatt are his Pinot Noirs: fresh and red fruited. Ask the sommelier about each before you describe them.

chateau-musar.name: Château Musar
chateau-musar.line: Lebanon's famous estate in the Bekaa Valley, releasing long lived reds only when it judges them ready.
chateau-musar.tell: Musar is the great wine of Lebanon, made by the Hochar family in the Bekaa Valley. The red blends Cabernet, Cinsault and Carignan and is released with age: spicy, earthy and layered, unlike any other wine. Hochar is the younger red. Older vintages are listed.

kracher.name: Kracher
kracher.line: A family estate by Lake Neusiedl, one of the great names in sweet wine.
kracher.tell: Kracher is a family estate by Lake Neusiedl, where autumn mists help sweet wine. The Auslese is honeyed and fresh, with apricot and citrus. A lovely partner for fruit desserts.

inniskillin.name: Inniskillin
inniskillin.line: A Niagara winery that helped make Canadian icewine famous.
inniskillin.tell: Inniskillin helped put Canadian icewine on the map. Icewine is made from grapes frozen on the vine. This one is Cabernet Franc: sweet, with strawberry and red berry flavours and bright acidity. A pretty match for fruit or chocolate desserts.

alberto-nanclares.name: Alberto Nanclares
alberto-nanclares.line: A small Galician grower best known for Albariño, also making red from Ribeira Sacra.
alberto-nanclares.tell: Alberto Nanclares is a small Galician grower known for fresh, natural minded Albariño. This red comes from Ribeira Sacra, steep river terraces inland: light, fresh and mineral. Ask the sommelier about the grape.

envinate.name: Envínate
envinate.line: A group of friends making fresh, low intervention wines from Atlantic and mountain vineyards across Spain.
envinate.tell: Envínate is four friends making wine in the Canary Islands, Galicia and Almansa. Their reds are fresh and savoury: Lousas is Mencía from Ribeira Sacra, Táganan, Benje and Migan come from volcanic Tenerife, and Albahra is Garnacha Tintorera. Light, smoky and lively, great with food.

guimaro.name: Guímaro
guimaro.line: A family estate on the steep slopes of Ribeira Sacra, making fresh Mencía.
guimaro.tell: Guímaro is a family estate in Ribeira Sacra, where vines grow on dizzying river terraces. Camino Real is a Mencía: fresh, peppery and red fruited, with mineral depth. A great swap for a Pinot or Cru Beaujolais lover.

la-perdida.name: La Perdida
la-perdida.line: A small natural minded producer in Valdeorras, inland Galicia.
la-perdida.tell: La Perdida is a small producer in Valdeorras, inland Galicia. O Trancado is a red from local grapes: fresh, light and savoury. An adventurous choice; ask the sommelier about the blend.

luis-rodriguez.name: Luis Rodríguez
luis-rodriguez.line: A Ribeiro grower who revived local grapes in this corner of Galicia.
luis-rodriguez.tell: Luis Rodríguez works with old local grapes in Ribeiro, Galicia. A Torna dos Pasás is a red: fresh, fragrant and lightly spicy. A fun, unusual pick for fish, pork or poultry.

d-ventura.name: D. Ventura
d-ventura.line: A small Ribeira Sacra producer bottling Mencía from single vineyards on the river slopes.
d-ventura.tell: D. Ventura bottles single vineyards in Ribeira Sacra. Viña Caneiro is a Mencía from steep slate slopes: fresh, red fruited and mineral. A light, lively red for food.

quinta-do-estranxeiro.name: Quinta do Estranxeiro
quinta-do-estranxeiro.line: A Ribeira Sacra project from the owners of Bodegas Zárate in Rías Baixas, working old bush vines on steep terraces.
quinta-do-estranxeiro.tell: Quinta do Estranxeiro is a young Ribeira Sacra project from the family behind Zárate, a top Albariño house. O Estranxeiro is mostly Mencía from old terraced vines: wild berries, herbs and a juicy texture. A fresh, food friendly red.

raul-perez.name: Raúl Pérez
raul-perez.line: An influential winemaker based in Bierzo who works with old vineyards across north west Spain.
raul-perez.tell: Raúl Pérez is one of the most influential winemakers in Spain, working old vines in Bierzo and Galicia. El Pecado is a Ribeira Sacra red: fragrant, mineral and fine. A treat for an adventurous guest.

akutain.name: Bodega Akutain
akutain.line: A small family bodega in Rioja.
akutain.tell: Akutain is a small family winery in Rioja. Expect classic Tempranillo: red fruit, spice and a touch of oak. Ask the sommelier about the ageing category of this bottle.

altos-ibericos.name: Altos Ibéricos
altos-ibericos.line: A Rioja label from the Torres family of Catalonia.
altos-ibericos.tell: Altos Ibéricos is the Torres family's Rioja. The Reserva is Tempranillo aged in oak: red fruit, vanilla and spice. A smooth, reliable Rioja at a fair price.

diego-magana.name: Diego Magaña
diego-magana.line: A small Rioja producer bottling single vineyard wines.
diego-magana.tell: Diego Magaña is a small Rioja producer. San Ginés is a single site red: classic Rioja fruit with a savoury edge. Ask the sommelier about its style before you describe it.

cvne.name: CVNE
cvne.line: A historic Rioja house in Haro, known for Imperial and Viña Real.
cvne.tell: CVNE, said coo-nay, is a historic house in Haro. Imperial is its classic Rioja Alta line, elegant and long lived; Viña Real is fuller, from Rioja Alavesa. Reserva and Gran Reserva bottles are aged long before release, smooth and savoury.

faustino.name: Bodegas Faustino
faustino.line: A large family house in Rioja Alavesa; Faustino I is its famous Gran Reserva.
faustino.tell: Faustino is a well known family house in Rioja. Faustino I Gran Reserva is aged for years before release: mellow, with dried cherry, leather and vanilla. A classic, mature Rioja at a fair price.

luberri.name: Bodegas Luberri
luberri.line: A family winery in Rioja Alavesa.
luberri.tell: Luberri is a family winery in Rioja Alavesa. Biga is a Tempranillo with some oak ageing: ripe, smooth and spicy. A friendly Rioja for lamb or pork.

contino.name: Contino
contino.line: A single estate in Rioja Alavesa, one of the first Rioja wines from one vineyard.
contino.tell: Contino is a single estate on a bend of the Ebro in Rioja Alavesa, unusual in a region of blends. The Gran Reserva is deep, fine and long lived. A great choice for a Rioja lover.

dominio-del-challao.name: Dominio del Challao
dominio-del-challao.line: A young biodynamic estate in Labastida, Rioja Alavesa, from a family with wineries in Bierzo and Argentina.
dominio-del-challao.tell: Challao is a young biodynamic estate in Labastida, Rioja Alavesa, worked partly with horses. Challao is a field blend led by Tempranillo; Vino de Labastida is the village wine. Fresh, modern, terroir minded Rioja.

la-rioja-alta.name: La Rioja Alta
la-rioja-alta.line: A classic Haro house famous for long aged Gran Reservas 890 and 904.
la-rioja-alta.tell: La Rioja Alta is a classic house in Haro. 904 and 890 are Gran Reservas aged for years in American oak: silky, savoury and complex, with dried cherry, leather and spice. 890 is the rarer one. Treasures for a Rioja lover.

lopez-de-heredia.name: López de Heredia
lopez-de-heredia.line: Rioja's great traditional house in Haro, ageing its wines for many years before release.
lopez-de-heredia.tell: López de Heredia is Rioja's most traditional house, ageing wines for years before release. Cubillo is the youngest red, a Crianza: fresh, savoury and gently mature. A wonderful introduction to old style Rioja.

marques-de-caceres.name: Marqués de Cáceres
marques-de-caceres.line: A well known Rioja house making classic Reservas and Gran Reservas.
marques-de-caceres.tell: Marqués de Cáceres is a widely known Rioja name. The Gran Reserva is aged long: smooth, with red fruit, vanilla and spice. A safe, classic choice.

remelluri.name: Remelluri
remelluri.line: A historic estate in the hills of Rioja Alavesa, run by the family of Telmo Rodríguez.
remelluri.tell: Remelluri is an estate high in Rioja Alavesa, farmed organically by the family of winemaker Telmo Rodríguez. The Reserva is fresh and savoury; the Gran Reserva in magnum is deeper and longer. Elegant Rioja for lamb.

valenciso.name: Valenciso
valenciso.line: A small Rioja estate making one elegant Reserva.
valenciso.tell: Valenciso is a small Rioja estate that focuses on a single Reserva: fresh, fine Tempranillo with gentle oak. A modern classic for lamb or pork.

clos-mogador.name: Clos Mogador
clos-mogador.line: One of the pioneering estates that revived Priorat in the late twentieth century.
clos-mogador.tell: Clos Mogador was one of the estates that brought Priorat back to fame. The wines grow on steep slate called llicorella: deep, mineral and powerful. Manyetes is mostly Carignan from one site. Big wines for lamb or beef.

costers-del-priorat.name: Costers del Priorat
costers-del-priorat.line: A Priorat producer working old vines on steep slopes, with minimal intervention.
costers-del-priorat.tell: Costers del Priorat works old vineyards in Priorat. Clos Alzina is Carignan from a high, north facing site planted long ago: fresh for Priorat, mineral and fine. A great pick for a curious red drinker.

familia-torres.name: Familia Torres
familia-torres.line: Spain's great family wine house, from Penedès, with estates across the country.
familia-torres.tell: Torres is Spain's best known wine family. Mas La Plana is their famous Penedès Cabernet; Salmos and Secret del Priorat come from Priorat, deep and mineral; Celeste is a Ribera del Duero Tempranillo. Reliable, quality reds at many price points.

la-vinya-del-vuit.name: La Vinya del Vuit
la-vinya-del-vuit.line: A small Priorat project making wine from old vines.
la-vinya-del-vuit.tell: La Vinya del Vuit is a small Priorat project. Expect a deep, mineral red from Garnacha and Carignan grown on slate. Ask the sommelier about the blend.

els-jelipins.name: Els Jelipins
els-jelipins.line: A tiny Penedès producer known for natural wine from the local Sumoll grape.
els-jelipins.tell: Els Jelipins is a tiny producer in Penedès, working the local red grape Sumoll in a natural way. The wine is fresh, wild and fragrant. A rare, adventurous pick.

antoine-graillot-raul-perez.name: Antoine Graillot and Raúl Pérez
antoine-graillot-raul-perez.line: A collaboration in Bierzo between a winemaker from the Rhône and Raúl Pérez.
antoine-graillot-raul-perez.tell: Encinas is a Bierzo red made as a collaboration between Antoine Graillot, from a Crozes-Hermitage family, and Raúl Pérez. Mencía from Bierzo: fresh, peppery and red fruited. A good swap for a Northern Rhône lover.

garmon.name: Bodegas Garmón
garmon.line: A Ribera del Duero estate making rich, polished Tempranillo.
garmon.tell: Garmón is a Ribera del Duero estate. The wine is Tempranillo, called Tinto Fino here: dark, ripe and polished, with firm tannin. Good with beef or lamb.

gregory-perez.name: Gregory Pérez (Brezo)
gregory-perez.line: A Bierzo winemaker whose Brezo label offers fresh, good value Mencía.
gregory-perez.tell: Brezo is Gregory Pérez's Bierzo Mencía: fresh, floral and red fruited, with a peppery lift. A great value, food friendly red, lovely with poultry or pork.

descendientes-de-j-palacios.name: Descendientes de J. Palacios
descendientes-de-j-palacios.line: The Palacios family estate in Bierzo, which helped make Mencía famous.
descendientes-de-j-palacios.tell: Descendientes de J. Palacios is the Bierzo estate of Ricardo Pérez Palacios and his uncle Álvaro Palacios. Corullón comes from old vines on steep slate: fresh, floral and mineral Mencía. A beautiful red for a Burgundy lover.

dominio-de-pingus.name: Dominio de Pingus
dominio-de-pingus.line: A cult Ribera del Duero estate founded by Peter Sisseck; Flor de Pingus is its second wine.
dominio-de-pingus.tell: Pingus is one of Spain's cult wines, made in tiny amounts by Peter Sisseck in Ribera del Duero. Flor de Pingus is the more available second wine: deep, dark and polished Tempranillo. A celebration red for beef.

la-vizcaina.name: La Vizcaína de Vinos
la-vizcaina.line: A Bierzo project from Raúl Pérez, bottling Mencía from single villages and vineyards.
la-vizcaina.tell: La Vizcaína is Raúl Pérez's Bierzo project. La Poulosa and Las Gundiñas are single vineyards: fresh, mineral Mencía with red fruit and spice. Great with poultry, pork or mushrooms.

vega-sicilia.name: Vega Sicilia
vega-sicilia.line: Spain's most famous estate, in Ribera del Duero; Unico is its legendary long aged red.
vega-sicilia.tell: Vega Sicilia is Spain's most famous wine. Unico is aged for years before release: complex, silky and very long lived. Reserva Especial blends several vintages, and Valbuena 5° is younger. Celebration bottles; involve the sommelier.

numanthia.name: Numanthia
numanthia.line: A Toro estate making powerful Tempranillo from old vines; Termanthia is its top wine.
numanthia.tell: Numanthia makes big reds in Toro, a hot region on the Duero. Termanthia is its flagship, from very old vines: dense, dark and powerful. For a guest who loves rich red with steak.

cuatro-monos.name: 4 Monos
cuatro-monos.line: A small group making fresh Garnacha from the mountains west of Madrid.
cuatro-monos.tell: 4 Monos, four monkeys, is a small project in the Sierra de Gredos west of Madrid. Vino de los Tres Pueblos is a Garnacha blend from three villages: fresh, red fruited and lightly herbal. A lovely, lighter red.

comando-g.name: Comando G
comando-g.line: A celebrated Sierra de Gredos project making fine, fragrant mountain Garnacha.
comando-g.tell: Comando G makes Garnacha in the granite mountains of the Sierra de Gredos, and it tastes more like Burgundy than big Spanish red: fragrant, fresh and fine. Las Iruelas, Navatalgordo, Rozas 1er and Tumba del Rey Moro are separate sites. A must for a curious Pinot lover.

jimenez-landi.name: Bodegas Jiménez-Landi
jimenez-landi.line: A family estate in the Sierra de Gredos making fresh, mountain Garnacha.
jimenez-landi.tell: Jiménez-Landi makes Garnacha in the Sierra de Gredos. El Reventón is a high altitude site: fresh, fragrant and fine, with red fruit and herbs. A great swap for a Pinot drinker.

hand-work.name: Hand Work
hand-work.line: An organic La Mancha label from the Parra brothers.
hand-work.tell: Hand Work is made by three brothers who farm organically in La Mancha. The Garnacha is juicy and bright, with red cherry and strawberry. A great value, easy red for casual dishes.

theopetra.name: Theopetra Estate
theopetra.line: A family estate in Meteora, central Greece, that revived the vineyards of the area.
theopetra.tell: Theopetra is a family estate below the rock pillars of Meteora in central Greece. 24 is named for its ageing: twenty four months in barrel and the same in bottle. A blend of Syrah, Cabernet and the local Limniona: dark berries, pepper and silky tannin.

thymiopoulos.name: Thymiopoulos
thymiopoulos.line: A leading Naoussa grower who made Xinomavro fresh and approachable.
thymiopoulos.tell: Thymiopoulos is the leading young name in Naoussa, northern Greece. Xinomavro is a firm, fragrant grape often compared to Nebbiolo. Young Vines is bright and juicy, with cherry and tomato leaf. A great value red for a curious guest.

luis-pato.name: Luis Pato
luis-pato.line: A leading Bairrada grower, champion of the firm, fresh Baga grape.
luis-pato.tell: Luis Pato is the name in Bairrada, near Portugal's Atlantic coast. Baga is a high acid, firm red grape. Quinta do Moinho is a single vineyard Baga: red fruit, earth and grip, lovely with roast meats.

mainova.name: Mainova
mainova.line: A young organic estate in the Alto Alentejo making wine with minimal intervention.
mainova.tell: Mainova is a young family estate in the Alto Alentejo, farmed organically. This red is Alicante Bouschet, a dark, deeply coloured grape that does well in Alentejo: dark berries and soft spice. A warm, generous red for meat.

niepoort.name: Niepoort
niepoort.line: A family Port house in Porto, also a leading maker of Douro and Bairrada table wines.
niepoort.tell: Niepoort is a family Port house known for its Colheitas and Garrafeira, tawny Ports from single vintages aged long. The Vintage Ports are deep and long lived. Lagar de Baixo is a Baga red from Bairrada: fresh and firm.

viuva-gomes.name: Viúva Gomes
viuva-gomes.line: A historic producer in Colares, where vines grow in sand by the Atlantic.
viuva-gomes.tell: Viúva Gomes makes wine in Colares, near Lisbon, where vines grow in deep sand by the ocean. Ramisco is the local red grape: firm, high in acid and long lived. A rare, historic wine; ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

catena-zapata.name: Catena Zapata
catena-zapata.line: The family that led Argentina to high altitude vineyards and world class Malbec.
catena-zapata.tell: Catena Zapata led the move to high altitude vineyards in Mendoza. Argentino is a Malbec blending several sites; River comes from the Adrianna Vineyard, very high up. Rich, dark and fresh. The half bottle Malbec suits two guests.

murdoch-hill.name: Murdoch Hill
murdoch-hill.line: A family estate in the cool Adelaide Hills, making fresh, bright wines.
murdoch-hill.tell: Murdoch Hill is a family estate in the Adelaide Hills, a cool part of South Australia. The Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and lively, with citrus and passion fruit. A good value white for seafood or salad.

canopus.name: Canopus
canopus.line: A small Mendoza producer making natural minded Malbec.
canopus.tell: Canopus is a small Mendoza producer. De Sed is a Malbec made with a light hand: fresh, juicy and floral, lighter than the classic style. A fun, good value red.

achaval-ferrer.name: Achával-Ferrer
achaval-ferrer.line: A Mendoza estate known for single vineyard Malbecs from old vines.
achaval-ferrer.tell: Achával-Ferrer bottles Malbec by vineyard: Finca Altamira, Finca Bella Vista and Finca Mirador. Each is concentrated and deep, with dark fruit and violet. A great comparison for a Malbec lover.

mendel.name: Mendel
mendel.line: A Mendoza winery working old vines in Luján de Cuyo.
mendel.tell: Mendel is a Mendoza winery known for old vines. Its Cabernet Sauvignon is ripe and polished, with dark fruit and fresh acidity. A good value alternative to Napa Cabernet.

cheval-des-andes.name: Cheval des Andes
cheval-des-andes.line: A partnership in Mendoza between Château Cheval Blanc and Terrazas de los Andes.
cheval-des-andes.tell: Cheval des Andes is a joint venture between Château Cheval Blanc of Saint-Émilion and Terrazas de los Andes. It is a Malbec blend: fine, polished and fresh, Bordeaux style with Argentine fruit. A great choice for a Bordeaux lover.

kaiken.name: Kaiken
kaiken.line: The Mendoza winery of Chilean winemaker Aurelio Montes.
kaiken.tell: Kaiken is the Argentine winery of the Montes family from Chile. Ultra is its Malbec: dark, ripe and smooth. A friendly, good value red for steak.

vina-cobos.name: Viña Cobos
vina-cobos.line: The Mendoza winery founded by Paul Hobbs, making rich, single vineyard Malbec.
vina-cobos.tell: Viña Cobos was founded by California winemaker Paul Hobbs. Chañares Estate and Marchiori Vineyard are single vineyard Malbecs: rich, dark and polished. Big reds for steak.

proyecto-las-compuertas.name: Proyecto Las Compuertas
proyecto-las-compuertas.line: An Argentine project focused on old vine Malbec and soil differences.
proyecto-las-compuertas.tell: Proyecto Las Compuertas makes Malbec with an eye on soil. Cinco Suelos means five soils, blending parcels from different ground: fresh, dark fruited and floral. Ask the sommelier about its style.

zuccardi.name: Zuccardi
zuccardi.line: A family winery in the Uco Valley known for fresh, terroir focused Malbec.
zuccardi.tell: Zuccardi is a family estate in the high Uco Valley. Piedra Infinita comes from stony soils in Paraje Altamira: fresh, mineral and fine, a lighter, more precise Malbec. A great pick for a guest who thinks Malbec is always heavy.

penalolen.name: Peñalolén
penalolen.line: A Maipo Valley label from the family behind Domus Aurea, making good value Cabernet.
penalolen.tell: Peñalolén comes from the same family estate as Domus Aurea, in the foothills of the Andes near Santiago. The Cabernet is fresh and dark fruited, with a hint of mint. A great value red for steak.

dakel.name: Dakél
dakel.line: A coastal Chilean project making single vineyard Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in the Itata Valley.
dakel.tell: Dakél makes Pinot Noir from a single vineyard near the Pacific in the Itata Valley, southern Chile, on granite soils. It is fresh and elegant, with red fruit and spice. A smart value Pinot.

domus-aurea.name: Domus Aurea
domus-aurea.line: A family estate in the foothills of the Andes near Santiago, making long lived Cabernet.
domus-aurea.tell: Domus Aurea is a family estate in Maipo Alto, at the foot of the Andes. The Cabernet is fresh and fine, with dark fruit and mint, and it ages well. A thoughtful alternative to Bordeaux.

tara.name: Tara
tara.line: Wines from the Atacama desert in northern Chile, among the driest places on earth.
tara.tell: Tara comes from the Atacama desert, where vines grow near the coast in salty, chalky soil. The Pinot Noir is fresh, light and savoury, quite unlike any other. A great conversation bottle for a curious guest.

vina-maquis.name: Viña Maquis
vina-maquis.line: A family estate in Colchagua making fresh Cabernet and Carmenère.
vina-maquis.tell: Maquis is a family estate in Colchagua, south of Santiago. The Cabernet is fresh and dark fruited; the Carmenère, Chile's signature grape, is supple, with red pepper and spice. Good value reds.

beaumont.name: Beaumont
beaumont.line: A family farm in Bot River, near the coast of the Western Cape.
beaumont.tell: Beaumont is a family farm in Bot River. Pinotage is South Africa's own grape, a cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault: dark berries and a little smoke. Theirs is fresh and balanced. A fun pick for a curious guest.

gabrielskloof.name: Gabriëlskloof
gabrielskloof.line: A Bot River estate making fresh, balanced wines.
gabrielskloof.tell: Gabriëlskloof is an estate in Bot River, near the cool coast. The Blend is a Bordeaux style red: dark fruit and fresh acidity. A good value alternative to Bordeaux.

sadie.name: Sadie Family Wines
sadie.line: Eben Sadie's Swartland estate, a leader of the new wave of South African wine.
sadie.tell: Sadie Family is the leading name of the Swartland. Columella is the red, Syrah led with other Rhône grapes: deep, fragrant and fine. A treat for a Rhône lover.

geyer-wine-co.name: Geyer Wine Co.
geyer-wine-co.line: A small Barossa producer making characterful reds.
geyer-wine-co.tell: Geyer Wine Co. is a small Barossa label. Big Easy is a Petit Verdot blend: dark, juicy and fun. A good value red with a New Orleans friendly name.

ochota-barrels.name: Ochota Barrels
ochota-barrels.line: An Adelaide Hills winery known for fresh, light, natural minded wines.
ochota-barrels.tell: Ochota Barrels is an Adelaide Hills label known for fresh, lively wines. The Green Room is a Grenache blend from McLaren Vale: bright, juicy and light, lovely a touch cool. A fun pick for poultry or pork.

amon-ra.name: Amon-Ra (Glaetzer)
amon-ra.line: A Barossa Shiraz from the Glaetzer family, made from old vines.
amon-ra.tell: Amon-Ra is the Glaetzer family's old vine Barossa Shiraz: dense, dark and rich, with blackberry and spice. A big wine for a guest who loves Australian Shiraz.

aphelion.name: Aphelion Wine Co.
aphelion.line: A McLaren Vale label devoted to Grenache from old bush vines.
aphelion.tell: Aphelion focuses on Grenache from old bush vines in McLaren Vale. Brini, Wait and Hickinbotham are separate vineyards, picked early for freshness: red fruit, spice and silky texture. Great for a Pinot or Rhône lover.

bindi.name: Bindi
bindi.line: A small family estate in the cool Macedon Ranges, making fine Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
bindi.tell: Bindi is a small estate in the Macedon Ranges, one of Australia's coolest regions. Dixon is a Pinot Noir: fine, fragrant and fresh. A treat for a Burgundy lover.

by-farr.name: By Farr
by-farr.line: A Geelong family estate known for Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Shiraz.
by-farr.tell: By Farr is a Geelong family estate. Its Shiraz blend is peppery and fresh, with dark fruit, more Rhône than Barossa. A thoughtful pick for lamb.

hickinbotham.name: Hickinbotham Clarendon Vineyard
hickinbotham.line: A historic hillside vineyard in Clarendon, McLaren Vale.
hickinbotham.tell: Hickinbotham is a historic vineyard on the hills of Clarendon in McLaren Vale. Trueman is its Cabernet Sauvignon: dark, firm and fresh. A good alternative to Bordeaux.

jauma.name: Jauma
jauma.line: A natural wine producer in the Adelaide Hills making light, juicy reds.
jauma.tell: Jauma makes natural wine in the Adelaide Hills. Birdsey is a Cabernet Franc from the Seaview area of McLaren Vale: light, juicy and lively. An adventurous pick, lovely slightly cool.

penfolds.name: Penfolds
penfolds.line: Australia's most famous wine house; Grange is its legendary Shiraz.
penfolds.tell: Penfolds is Australia's most famous name. Grange is its iconic Shiraz: dense, dark and very long lived. Bin 389, a Cabernet Shiraz blend, is nicknamed baby Grange. Celebration bottles; decant.

seppeltsfield.name: Seppeltsfield
seppeltsfield.line: A historic Barossa estate, famous for fortified wines, also making reds.
seppeltsfield.tell: Seppeltsfield is a historic Barossa estate, famous for its aged fortified wines. Great Terraced Vineyard is a Grenache, fresh and fragrant; The Nothing is a Shiraz. Ask the sommelier about each.

thorn-clarke.name: Thorn-Clarke
thorn-clarke.line: A Barossa family winery making good value Shiraz.
thorn-clarke.tell: Thorn-Clarke is a family winery in the Barossa. Shotfire Ridge Shiraz is ripe, dark and smooth. A great value Australian red for steak.

timo-mayer.name: Timo Mayer
timo-mayer.line: A Yarra Valley winemaker known for fresh, whole bunch, natural minded reds.
timo-mayer.tell: Timo Mayer makes wine in the Yarra Valley with whole bunches and a light hand. His Syrah is fresh, peppery and fragrant, nothing like big Barossa Shiraz. A great pick for a Northern Rhône lover.

torbreck.name: Torbreck
torbreck.line: A Barossa estate known for old vine Shiraz and Rhône grapes.
torbreck.tell: Torbreck makes rich Barossa wine from old vines. The Factor is a Shiraz: dense, dark and spicy, with great depth. For a guest who loves big Australian red.

tyrrells.name: Tyrrell's
tyrrells.line: A Hunter Valley family house famous for Semillon and medium bodied Shiraz.
tyrrells.tell: Tyrrell's is a family house in the Hunter Valley. Vat 9 is its Shiraz, labelled Syrah here: medium bodied, earthy and fresh, very different from the Barossa. Ages beautifully.

burn-cottage.name: Burn Cottage
burn-cottage.line: A biodynamic estate in Central Otago making fine Pinot Noir.
burn-cottage.tell: Burn Cottage is a biodynamic estate in Central Otago, in the mountains of New Zealand's South Island. Its Pinot Noir is fine and fragrant; Moonlight Race is a second bottling. A strong Burgundy alternative.

dog-point.name: Dog Point Vineyard
dog-point.line: A Marlborough estate run by two families, known for Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.
dog-point.tell: Dog Point is a family estate in Marlborough. The Pinot Noir is fresh and savoury, with red cherry and spice. A good value Pinot for salmon or duck.

te-mata.name: Te Mata
te-mata.line: A historic Hawke's Bay estate known for Bordeaux style reds.
te-mata.tell: Te Mata is one of New Zealand's oldest estates, in Hawke's Bay. Awatea is a Cabernet Merlot blend: fresh, fine and fragrant. A good value Bordeaux alternative.

broadbent.name: Broadbent
broadbent.line: A Madeira label from wine importer Bartholomew Broadbent, here as single cask bottlings.
broadbent.tell: Broadbent bottles Madeira, the fortified wine of the Atlantic island, aged in warm conditions. Malvasia is the richest and sweetest style; Verdelho is medium dry. Both have burnt sugar, nut and citrus notes, with bright acidity. In 500 ml bottles.

henriques-and-henriques.name: Henriques & Henriques
henriques-and-henriques.tell: Henriques & Henriques is a classic Madeira house. Founder's Solera Verdelho is medium dry: nutty, tangy and caramel edged, with bright acidity. Lovely with nuts, cheese or a light dessert.

barbadillo.name: Barbadillo
barbadillo.line: A large Sherry house in Sanlúcar de Barrameda.
barbadillo.tell: Barbadillo is a big Sherry house in Sanlúcar. Pale Cream is a sweetened pale Sherry: light, nutty and gently sweet. Serve chilled with dessert or as an aperitif.

valdespino.name: Valdespino
valdespino.line: A historic Jerez Sherry house known for old, very long aged wines.
valdespino.tell: Valdespino is one of the oldest Sherry houses in Jerez. VOS Solera 1842 is a very old Sherry from Palomino: deep, nutty and complex. Ask the sommelier how sweet it is before you pour; in 500 ml bottles.

la-cigarrera.name: La Cigarrera
la-cigarrera.line: A small family Sherry house in Sanlúcar, making Manzanilla.
la-cigarrera.tell: La Cigarrera is a small family house in Sanlúcar. Manzanilla is the driest, freshest Sherry: salty, tangy and almondy. Serve chilled, with oysters, fried seafood or salty snacks.

cockburns.name: Cockburn's
cockburns.line: A historic Port house, known for its Vintage Ports.
cockburns.tell: Cockburn's is a historic Port house. Vintage Port is made only in the best years and aged in bottle: dark, rich and sweet. Older vintages need decanting; ask the sommelier.

c-da-silva.name: C. da Silva (Dalva)
c-da-silva.line: A Port house whose Dalva brand is known for aged tawny and Colheita Ports.
c-da-silva.tell: Dalva is the brand of C. da Silva, known for aged tawny Ports from single vintages. Expect nuts, dried fruit and caramel. Lovely with pecan or chocolate desserts; ask about the vintage.

dows.name: Dow's
dows.line: A great Port house of the Symington family, known for drier styled Vintage Ports.
dows.tell: Dow's is one of the great Port houses, known for a slightly drier finish than most. The Vintage Ports are dark and firm, and the list holds several years and a half bottle. Decant older bottles.

feist.name: Feist
feist.line: A Port house known mainly for ruby and tawny Ports.
feist.tell: Feist is a Port house known for ruby and tawny styles. Late Bottled Vintage Port is from a single year, aged longer in wood before bottling: rich, dark and ready to drink. Good with chocolate desserts.

grahams.name: Graham's
grahams.line: A great Port house of the Symington family, known for rich, sweet Vintage Ports.
grahams.tell: Graham's is one of the great Port names, known for a rich, sweet style. The Vintage Ports are dark and luscious, and several years are listed. Decant older bottles; wonderful with chocolate or blue cheese.

sandeman.name: Sandeman
sandeman.line: A historic Port house, famous for its caped figure logo.
sandeman.tell: Sandeman is a historic Port house guests recognise from the caped figure on its label. Late Bottled Vintage is rich and ready to drink; the Vintage Port is deeper and needs decanting.

smith-woodhouse.name: Smith Woodhouse
smith-woodhouse.line: A traditional Port house of the Symington family.
smith-woodhouse.tell: Smith Woodhouse is a traditional Port house, often good value. The Vintage Port is dark, rich and firm. Decant older bottles.

taylor-fladgate.name: Taylor Fladgate
taylor-fladgate.line: One of the great Port houses; Quinta de Vargellas is its famous estate.
taylor-fladgate.tell: Taylor Fladgate is one of the most famous Port houses. Its Vintage Ports are firm and long lived; Quinta de Vargellas is a single estate Vintage Port, made in years that are not declared. Decant older bottles.

warres.name: Warre's
warres.line: One of the oldest British Port houses, part of the Symington family.
warres.tell: Warre's is one of the oldest Port houses. The Vintage Port is fragrant and elegant, with dark fruit. Decant older bottles; lovely with chocolate or cheese.

domaine-huet.name: Domaine Huet
domaine-huet.line: Vouvray's reference estate, biodynamic, bottling three great vineyards from dry to sweet.
domaine-huet.tell: Huet is the name in Vouvray. It bottles three vineyards, Le Haut-Lieu, Le Mont and Clos du Bourg, and each comes Sec (dry), Demi-Sec (gently sweet) or Moelleux (sweet). Always say which style before pouring; the sweeter ones love spice.

el-enemigo.name: El Enemigo
el-enemigo.line: A Mendoza project of Alejandro Vigil and Adrianna Catena.
el-enemigo.tell: El Enemigo is a Mendoza project of Alejandro Vigil and Adrianna Catena. Its Chardonnay is fresh and good value.

liger-belair.name: Liger-Belair
liger-belair.line: A family name in the Côte de Nuits shared by two separate estates.
liger-belair.tell: Two Burgundy estates carry the Liger-Belair name, so ask the sommelier which one made this Aligoté. Expect a crisp, lemony white, a fresh start to a meal.

roco.name: Roco
roco.tell: Roco is a Willamette Valley winery. Gravel Road is a Chardonnay, fresh and bright.

sandhi.name: Sandhi
sandhi.line: A Sta. Rita Hills winery making lean, mineral Chardonnay.
sandhi.tell: Sandhi makes taut, mineral Chardonnay in the Sta. Rita Hills. Sanford & Benedict and La Rinconada are famous vineyards, and the Central Coast bottling is the value entry.

sylvaine-alain-normand.name: Sylvaine et Alain Normand
sylvaine-alain-normand.line: A family estate in the Mâconnais making fresh Chardonnay.
sylvaine-alain-normand.tell: The Normands are a family estate in the Mâconnais in southern Burgundy. Their Bourgogne is fresh, gentle Chardonnay at a fair price.

the-paring.name: The Paring
the-paring.tell: The Paring is a Santa Barbara label. This Chardonnay is fresh and fruity, an easy, good-value white.

dirler-cade.name: Dirler-Cadé
dirler-cade.line: A biodynamic family estate in Bergholtz in southern Alsace.
dirler-cade.tell: Dirler-Cadé is a biodynamic family estate in southern Alsace. Edelzwicker is a traditional blend of Alsace grapes: aromatic, fresh and easy.

loimer.name: Loimer
loimer.tell: Loimer is a biodynamic estate in the Kamptal. Lois is a fresh, peppery Grüner Veltliner, crisp and good value.

sylvain-morey.name: Sylvain Morey
sylvain-morey.line: A Burgundian making wine in the Luberon.
sylvain-morey.tell: Sylvain Morey comes from a Burgundy family and makes wine in the Luberon. Panorama is a white, fresh and round, and good value.

mas-de-valeriole.name: Mas de Valériole
mas-de-valeriole.tell: Valériole is an estate in the Camargue. Vé is a pale, dry rosé, offered in bottle and magnum.

faiveley.name: Domaine Faiveley
faiveley.line: A historic Nuits-Saint-Georges house and one of Burgundy's biggest vineyard owners, making structured, modern, well made reds from Mercurey to Chambertin.
faiveley.tell: Faiveley owns a remarkable spread of vineyards, many in the Côte de Nuits and the Côte Chalonnaise. The reds are dark, firm and reliable, from Mercurey up to the Chambertin grand crus. A safe, quality recommendation at almost any price.

louis-jadot.name: Louis Jadot
louis-jadot.line: One of the great Beaune houses, owning large holdings across the Côte d'Or and Beaujolais and bottling an enormous range of reds.
louis-jadot.tell: Jadot is one of Burgundy's most recognised names, owning vineyards from Beaujolais up to Chambertin. The quality is very consistent, and bottles marked Domaine come from their own vineyards. The half bottle is a handy option for a couple.

ferrari.name: Ferrari
ferrari.line: A family-owned house in Trento making traditional method sparkling wine from mountain vineyards.
ferrari.tell: Ferrari, no relation to the cars, is Trento's great sparkling house. The Brut is crisp and appley; Perlé is a vintage Blanc de Blancs; the Rosé is fruity and dry. The half-bottle suits one or two.

krug.name: Krug
krug.line: The Reims house that ferments in small oak casks and builds Grande Cuvée from many vintages, numbered by edition.
krug.tell: Krug is barrel-fermented and deeply complex, toasty, nutty and powerful. Grande Cuvée blends over a hundred wines from many years; the edition number tells you which. Clos du Mesnil and Clos d'Ambonnay are tiny walled vineyards, among Champagne's rarest bottles.

laurent-perrier.name: Laurent-Perrier
laurent-perrier.line: A Tours-sur-Marne house known for its rosé made by skin maceration and for Grand Siècle, a blend of three vintages.
laurent-perrier.tell: Laurent-Perrier is famous for its rosé, coloured by soaking Pinot Noir on its skins, and for Grand Siècle, which blends three great vintages; the Iteration number names the release. Harmony is a demi-sec, sweeter, for dessert.

nicolas-feuillatte.name: Nicolas Feuillatte
nicolas-feuillatte.line: A large growers' cooperative brand in Chouilly, fresh and fruity, with Palmes d'Or as its prestige cuvée.
nicolas-feuillatte.tell: Nicolas Feuillatte brings together grapes from thousands of growers through a cooperative. The Réserve is fresh, fruity and approachable; Palmes d'Or is the prestige vintage in its studded bottle, and comes as a fuller rosé too.

veuve-fourny.name: Veuve Fourny & Fils
veuve-fourny.line: A family house in Vertus run by two brothers, making crisp, low-dosage premier cru Chardonnay.
veuve-fourny.tell: Veuve Fourny is a family house in Vertus. The wines are dry and chalky; Monts de Vertus is a single site; the half-bottles suit one or two guests; Vinothèque MV2000 is a perpetual-reserve blend in magnum.

schramsberg.name: Schramsberg
schramsberg.line: A historic Calistoga estate devoted to traditional method sparkling wine.
schramsberg.tell: Schramsberg is a Napa sparkling estate with historic caves. The Blanc de Blancs is crisp and lively, here in half-bottle; J. Schram is the prestige wine, richer and longer.

louis-michel.name: Domaine Louis Michel
louis-michel.line: A Chablis estate that ages in steel rather than oak, giving pure, crisp, mineral wines.
louis-michel.tell: Louis Michel uses no oak, so the wines are pure Chablis: crisp, lemony and stony. Grenouilles is a grand cru; Montmains a premier cru in half-bottle. Ideal with oysters and shellfish.

matrot.name: Domaine Matrot
matrot.line: A traditional Meursault estate run by Thierry and Pascale Matrot's family.
matrot.tell: Matrot is a traditional Meursault estate. Charmes and Perrières are premier crus, and the half-bottle Bourgogne suits one or two guests.

donnhoff.name: Dönnhoff
donnhoff.tell: Dönnhoff is the Nahe's greatest name. Hermannshöhle and Brücke are famous sites; the GG is dry, while Spätlese and Auslese are sweeter.

dr-hermann.name: Dr. Hermann
dr-hermann.tell: Dr. Hermann is a family estate in Erden on the Mosel. The Spätlese and Auslese bottles are sweeter Rieslings, lovely with spice or dessert.

keller.name: Keller
keller.tell: Keller is a cult name in Rheinhessen. Von der Fels is dry and Limestone Kabinett gently sweet, while Morstein and Hubacker GG are dry grand crus and very sought after.

schloss-gobelsburg.name: Schloss Gobelsburg
schloss-gobelsburg.line: A historic Kamptal estate with monastic roots, known for Riesling, Grüner Veltliner and the old-style Tradition wines.
schloss-gobelsburg.tell: Schloss Gobelsburg is a historic estate in the Kamptal. The Heiligenstein Riesling is mineral and fine; Tradition is a Grüner-based wine made in an old-fashioned way, aged long in big casks. Their Brut is crisp and elegant.

chalk-hill.name: Chalk Hill
chalk-hill.line: A Sonoma estate in its own small appellation, known for rich Chardonnay.
chalk-hill.tell: Chalk Hill is a Sonoma estate known for Chardonnay. Expect a round, ripe style with toasty oak. Here in half-bottle, right for one or two guests.

bitouzet-prieur.name: Bitouzet-Prieur
bitouzet-prieur.line: A family domaine straddling Volnay and Meursault, making traditional, quietly classic Volnay and white Meursault.
bitouzet-prieur.tell: A traditional family estate. Their Volnay is the elegant, perfumed style the village is known for: red fruit, silky tannin, nothing forced. With some age now, it is a lovely partner for poultry and veal.

bouchard-pere-et-fils.name: Bouchard Père & Fils
bouchard-pere-et-fils.line: One of the largest landholders on the Côte d'Or, a historic Beaune house whose own premier and grand cru vineyards anchor a broad range.
bouchard-pere-et-fils.tell: Bouchard owns a large spread of top vineyards, especially in Beaune. Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus is their famous parcel in the Beaune Grèves premier cru. The half bottles here are a handy way to give a couple a proper premier cru Burgundy.

chateau-leoville-las-cases.name: Château Léoville Las Cases
chateau-leoville-las-cases.line: A Saint-Julien second growth run by the Delon family, beside Latour, often ranked with the first growths for power and longevity.
chateau-leoville-las-cases.tell: Las Cases is one of the most prestigious second growths, its Grand Enclos running right up to Latour. The wine is serious and long lived. Decant, and give it time in the glass.

chateau-lynch-bages.name: Château Lynch-Bages
chateau-lynch-bages.line: A Pauillac fifth growth owned by the Cazes family, much loved for rich, generous, cassis rich wine that drinks above its rank.
chateau-lynch-bages.tell: Lynch-Bages is one of the most loved names in Bordeaux, often compared with second growths. Rich, generous Cabernet with cassis and cedar. The magnum is a great pick for a celebration.

chateau-montrose.name: Château Montrose
chateau-montrose.line: A Saint-Estèphe second growth on gravel near the Gironde estuary, known for powerful, long lived Cabernet led wines.
chateau-montrose.tell: Montrose overlooks the Gironde and makes one of the most powerful wines of the Médoc. It needs time and rewards it. Decant, and pair with beef or lamb.

chateau-mouton-rothschild.name: Château Mouton Rothschild
chateau-mouton-rothschild.line: The Pauillac first growth, promoted in 1973, famous for its rich, opulent wine and labels painted by a different artist each year.
chateau-mouton-rothschild.tell: Mouton is the first growth with an artist's label every year, a great story at the table. The wine is rich and opulent. Ask the sommelier who painted this vintage's label, and decant.

chateau-pichon-lalande.name: Château Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande
chateau-pichon-lalande.line: A Pauillac second growth facing Latour, owned by the Roederer Champagne family, known for silky, perfumed, Merlot rich Pauillac.
chateau-pichon-lalande.tell: Pichon Lalande is one of the most elegant Pauillacs, with more Merlot than most, which gives a silky texture. The half bottle is a beautiful option for two.

chateau-troplong-mondot.name: Château Troplong-Mondot
chateau-troplong-mondot.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé on a high point of the appellation.
chateau-troplong-mondot.tell: Troplong-Mondot sits on one of the highest points in Saint-Émilion. The half bottle is a lovely treat for two.

henri-gouges.name: Domaine Henri Gouges
henri-gouges.line: The reference domaine of Nuits-Saint-Georges, making firm, dark, long lived reds from the village's best premier crus.
henri-gouges.tell: Gouges is the name most people think of in Nuits-Saint-Georges. The wines are sturdy and structured, with dark fruit and an earthy edge, and they age very well. The half bottles are a great option for two guests with red meat.

raspail-ay.name: Domaine Raspail-Ay
raspail-ay.tell: Raspail-Ay is a traditional Gigondas family. Expect a warm, spicy red. The half bottle is handy for a couple.

famille-perrin.name: Famille Perrin
famille-perrin.line: The Perrin family's négociant range, from the owners of Château de Beaucastel.
famille-perrin.tell: The Perrin family, of Beaucastel, make this Côtes du Rhône-Villages. The half bottle is a handy, easy red.

tollot-beaut.name: Domaine Tollot-Beaut
tollot-beaut.line: A Chorey-lès-Beaune family domaine making ripe, generous reds from Chorey, Savigny, Beaune, Aloxe-Corton and Corton.
tollot-beaut.tell: Tollot-Beaut is a reliable family estate known for ripe, fruity, crowd pleasing reds. Chorey-lès-Beaune is one of the best values on the list, and the Corton Bressandes is a step up. Safe recommendations.

vieux-chateau-certan.name: Vieux Château Certan
vieux-chateau-certan.line: A Pomerol estate run by the Thienpont family, with more Cabernet Franc than most, making fine, fragrant wine.
vieux-chateau-certan.tell: Vieux Château Certan, run by the Thienpont family, is one of Pomerol's great names. The half bottle is a lovely treat for two.

billecart-salmon.name: Billecart-Salmon
billecart-salmon.line: A family-run house in Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, prized for finesse, freshness and one of Champagne's most admired rosés.
billecart-salmon.tell: Billecart-Salmon is still family run and loved for elegance: fine bubbles, fresh fruit and a clean finish. The rosé is the one guests know; Elisabeth Salmon is its prestige rosé, Nicolas François the prestige white, and Clos St Hilaire a rare single vineyard Pinot Noir.

bollinger.name: Bollinger
bollinger.line: A family house in Aÿ with a rich, Pinot Noir-led style shaped by barrel fermentation and long ageing.
bollinger.tell: Bollinger is Pinot Noir country Champagne: full, toasty and vinous, partly fermented in oak. Special Cuvée is the house blend, La Grande Année the vintage, R.D. a vintage aged long on its lees and disgorged late, and Vieilles Vignes Françaises a tiny, legendary Blanc de Noirs.

caillez-lemaire.name: Caillez Lemaire
caillez-lemaire.line: A family grower in Damery in the Marne valley, with a low-dosage, Meunier-rich style.
caillez-lemaire.tell: Caillez Lemaire is a family estate in Damery. Pur is a Blanc de Noirs with no added sugar, crisp and fruity; Éclats is the blend, here in magnum, which suits a table of four or more.

charles-heidsieck.name: Charles Heidsieck
charles-heidsieck.line: A Reims house famous for using a high share of old reserve wines, giving rich, toasty, creamy Champagne.
charles-heidsieck.tell: Charles Heidsieck ages its wines in old chalk cellars and blends in a lot of older reserve wine, so even the Brut Réserve tastes rich and toasty. Blanc des Millénaires is the long-aged prestige Blanc de Blancs; Champagne Charlie revives a historic name.

delamotte.name: Delamotte
delamotte.line: A small Le Mesnil-sur-Oger house, sister to Salon, devoted to Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs.
delamotte.tell: Delamotte is Salon's sister house in Le Mesnil, heart of the Côte des Blancs. Its Blanc de Blancs is crisp, chalky and elegant, with lemon and brioche, a great step toward Salon's style at a gentler price.

diebolt-vallois.name: Diebolt-Vallois
diebolt-vallois.line: A family grower in Cramant making fine, creamy Blanc de Blancs.
diebolt-vallois.tell: Diebolt-Vallois is a family estate in Cramant, a grand cru for Chardonnay. The Blanc de Blancs is fine, floral and creamy; here in magnum for a larger table.

ruinart.name: Ruinart
ruinart.line: Founded in 1729 and often called the oldest established Champagne house, Ruinart is known for Chardonnay.
ruinart.tell: Ruinart dates to 1729 and leans on Chardonnay for a fresh, bright style. Dom Ruinart is the prestige vintage, a long-aged Blanc de Blancs, with a rosé version too. The house rosé is fruity and soft.

drappier.name: Drappier
drappier.line: A family house in the Aube, deep in Pinot Noir country, with a lightly dosed style and a love of large bottles.
drappier.tell: Drappier is a family house in the Côte des Bar in the south of Champagne, where Pinot Noir rules. The wines are fruit-driven and often low in added sugar; Brut Nature has none. Grande Sendrée is their prestige vintage.

henri-giraud.name: Henri Giraud
henri-giraud.line: An old Aÿ family house that ages its wines in oak from the nearby Argonne forest.
henri-giraud.tell: Henri Giraud is a family house in Aÿ that ferments and ages in casks made from Argonne oak, close to Champagne. The wines are rich, vinous and nutty; Argonne is the top cuvée and Fût de Chêne the oak-aged blend.

gamet.name: Gamet
gamet.line: A family grower in the Marne valley; Rive Gauche is its left-bank blend, here in magnum.
gamet.tell: Gamet is a family estate in the Marne valley. Rive Gauche is a blend from the river's left bank, here in magnum. Ask the sommelier for the grape mix before you describe it in detail.

gaston-chiquet.name: Gaston Chiquet
gaston-chiquet.line: A Dizy family grower known for a rare Blanc de Blancs from Aÿ, a village planted mostly to Pinot Noir.
gaston-chiquet.tell: Gaston Chiquet is a family estate in Dizy. Their Blanc de Blancs d'Aÿ is unusual: Chardonnay from Aÿ, where Pinot Noir dominates, so it is fuller and rounder than a Côte des Blancs Chardonnay. Here in magnum.

gosset.name: Gosset
gosset.line: An Aÿ house that traces its wine roots to 1584 and usually avoids malolactic fermentation, keeping wines taut and fresh.
gosset.tell: Gosset claims to be the oldest wine house in Champagne and makes wines with bright, firm acidity because it usually blocks the softening malolactic step. Grande Réserve is the house blend; Celebris is the prestige vintage. Ideal with rich food.

henriot.name: Henriot
henriot.line: A Reims family house with a Chardonnay-rich style, fine and lightly toasty.
henriot.tell: Henriot leans on Chardonnay for a fine, creamy, lightly toasty style. The Blanc de Blancs is crisp; the Millésime is the vintage; Cuvée des Enchanteleurs and Hemera are the long-aged prestige wines.

jean-laurent.name: Jean Laurent
jean-laurent.line: A family grower in the Aube making Pinot Noir and Chardonnay Champagne, including rosé.
jean-laurent.tell: Jean Laurent is a family estate in the Côte des Bar. The rosé is fruity and full; the Blanc de Blancs, here in magnum, is fresher. Good value next to the big houses.

leclerc-briant.name: Leclerc Briant
leclerc-briant.line: An Épernay house that was an early convert to biodynamic farming, making pure, low-dosage wines.
leclerc-briant.tell: Leclerc Briant is an Épernay house known for organic and biodynamic farming. The wines are fresh and dry; Clos des Trois Clochers is a single walled vineyard with no added sugar; the Réserve, here in magnum, is the house blend.

louis-roederer.name: Louis Roederer
louis-roederer.line: A family-owned Reims house, maker of Cristal, with a precise, vinous style.
louis-roederer.tell: Roederer is family owned and farms most of its own vines. Cristal, first made for the Russian tsar, is the prestige wine: fine, chalky, long. Collection is the newer multi-vintage house blend, numbered by release.

perrier-jouet.name: Perrier-Jouët
perrier-jouet.line: An Épernay house with a floral, Chardonnay-led style; Belle Epoque wears the painted anemone bottle.
perrier-jouet.tell: Perrier-Jouët is all about elegance and flowers, built on Chardonnay. Belle Epoque, the vintage prestige wine in the anemone bottle, is the one guests recognise; it is delicate and creamy and photographs beautifully at the table.

pierre-peters.name: Pierre Péters
pierre-peters.line: A leading Le Mesnil grower whose Blanc de Blancs draws on a long-kept perpetual reserve.
pierre-peters.tell: Pierre Péters is one of the benchmark growers of Le Mesnil. Cuvée de Réserve blends young wine with a perpetual reserve, giving depth to its chalky freshness. Les Montjolys and Réserve Oubliée are the top bottles.

piper-heidsieck.name: Piper-Heidsieck
piper-heidsieck.line: A large Reims house with a fruity, Pinot Noir-led style; it makes Brennan's own Essential cuvée.
piper-heidsieck.tell: Piper-Heidsieck is a big Reims house with a generous, fruit-forward style led by Pinot Noir. Brennan's Essential is made for the house by Piper, an Extra Brut, so it is drier than most; the Sauvage rosé is fuller and fruitier.

rare-champagne.name: Rare Champagne
rare-champagne.line: Once Piper-Heidsieck's prestige cuvée, Rare is now its own label: vintage Champagne, rich and spicy, made only in chosen years.
rare-champagne.tell: Rare began as the prestige wine of Piper-Heidsieck and now stands on its own. It is made only in chosen vintages and aged long before release, so it tastes rich and layered, with toast, dried fruit and spice. A celebration bottle.

roland-champion.name: Roland Champion
roland-champion.line: A family grower in Chouilly making grand cru Blanc de Blancs.
roland-champion.tell: Roland Champion is a family estate in Chouilly. Grand Éclat is a grand cru Blanc de Blancs, here in a six-litre Methuselah, a bottle for a big celebration that needs planning with the sommelier.

salon.name: Salon
salon.line: Single cru, single grape, single vintage: Salon is Chardonnay from Le Mesnil, made only in exceptional years.
salon.tell: Salon makes one wine: a Blanc de Blancs from Le Mesnil, only in the finest years and aged about a decade before release. It is intense, chalky and long, one of the rarest Champagnes. Delamotte is its sister house.

taittinger.name: Taittinger
taittinger.line: A Reims house with a Chardonnay-rich, light and elegant style; Comtes de Champagne is its Blanc de Blancs.
taittinger.tell: Taittinger favours Chardonnay, so its wines are light, fine and elegant. La Française is the house Brut; Comtes de Champagne, the prestige Blanc de Blancs, is creamy and refined; the Prestige rosé is fresh and fruity.

brundlmayer.name: Bründlmayer
brundlmayer.line: A leading Kamptal estate in Langenlois, famous for Riesling from the Heiligenstein and Grüner Veltliner, plus fine sparkling wine.
brundlmayer.tell: Bründlmayer is one of Austria's great names. The Heiligenstein Rieslings are taut and mineral, the Grüner Veltliners peppery and fresh. Their sparkling wine is made the Champagne way and is among the best outside Champagne.

far-niente.name: Far Niente
far-niente.line: An Oakville estate that makes only Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon.
far-niente.tell: Far Niente is an Oakville estate that makes just Chardonnay and Cabernet. The Chardonnay is rich and creamy, with polished oak, here in magnum for a larger table.

hirsch.name: Weingut Hirsch
hirsch.line: A Kamptal family estate, organic and biodynamic, known for Heiligenstein Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
hirsch.tell: Hirsch is an organic family estate in the Kamptal. Lamm is a Grüner Veltliner site, and Gaisberg and Heiligenstein are Riesling sites: crisp, mineral and precise.

jj-prum.name: Joh. Jos. Prüm
jj-prum.tell: JJ Prüm is a legendary Mosel name. Wehlener Sonnenuhr Kabinett is light and gently sweet, and it ages beautifully.

billaud-simon.name: Billaud-Simon
billaud-simon.line: A historic Chablis estate known for pure, crisp wines, now owned by Faiveley.
billaud-simon.tell: Billaud-Simon is a historic Chablis estate, now owned by Faiveley. Vaillons is a premier cru, and the village Chablis, also in magnum, is crisp, fresh and lemony.

carrette.name: Domaine Carrette
carrette.tell: Carrette is a family estate in Pouilly-Fuissé in southern Burgundy. Les Crays is a single site, here in magnum: ripe and round.

domaine-de-la-mandeliere.name: Domaine de la Mandelière
domaine-de-la-mandeliere.line: A Chablis estate; Les Fourneaux is a premier cru, here in magnum.
domaine-de-la-mandeliere.tell: This is a Chablis premier cru, Les Fourneaux, in magnum. Expect crisp, stony Chardonnay without heavy oak, a good bottle to share around a table of oysters.

florent-garaudet.name: Domaine Florent Garaudet
florent-garaudet.line: A small estate in Monthelie making Meursault.
florent-garaudet.tell: Garaudet is a small estate based in Monthelie. This is a village Meursault from old vines, here in magnum for a table to share.

domaine-de-la-pepiere.name: Domaine de la Pépière
domaine-de-la-pepiere.line: A benchmark Muscadet estate making crisp, mineral, long-lived wines from old vines and named crus.
