domaine-de-la-pepiere.tell: Pépière is one of the estates that made people take Muscadet seriously. Château-Thébaud and Monnières-Saint-Fiacre are crus, aged longer on their lees: crisp, saline and deep. Perfect with raw oysters; magnums suit a table.

trimbach.name: Trimbach
trimbach.line: A historic Ribeauvillé house famous for dry, firm, long-lived Riesling, above all Clos Ste Hune.
trimbach.tell: Trimbach makes dry, firm Alsace whites. Clos Ste Hune is one of the world's great Rieslings, from a tiny plot; Cuvée Frédéric Emile is its other top Riesling; Vendanges Tardives means late harvest and is sweeter.

jean-collet.name: Domaine Jean Collet et Fils
jean-collet.line: A family estate in Chablis with grand and premier cru holdings.
jean-collet.tell: Collet is a family estate in Chablis. Valmur is a grand cru, Vaillons a premier cru, here in magnum; the village Chablis is crisp and fresh.

weinbach.name: Domaine Weinbach
weinbach.line: A celebrated family estate in Kaysersberg, around the walled Clos des Capucins, making rich, pure whites.
weinbach.tell: Weinbach is one of Alsace's great family estates. Clos des Capucins is the walled vineyard by the house; Schlossberg and Mambourg are grand crus; Cuvée Théo and Sainte Catherine are named cuvées. Aromatic and generous.

vatan.name: Edmond et Anne Vatan
vatan.line: A tiny, revered Chavignol estate whose Clos la Néore is one of Sancerre's most sought-after wines.
vatan.tell: Vatan is tiny and revered. Clos la Néore is Sancerre of great depth, made traditionally, with more texture and age-worthiness than most. Here in magnum, a rare find.

grange-des-peres.name: Domaine de la Grange des Pères
grange-des-peres.line: The cult Languedoc estate of Laurent Vaillé, blending Syrah, Mourvèdre and Cabernet Sauvignon.
grange-des-peres.tell: Grange des Pères is the cult wine of the Languedoc. Deep, fine and long lived. Rare bottles; decant.

marchand-tawse.name: Marchand-Tawse
marchand-tawse.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges house making wines across Burgundy.
marchand-tawse.tell: Marchand-Tawse is a Nuits-Saint-Georges house making wines across Burgundy. Genevrières is a Meursault premier cru, here in double magnum, and the village Meursault comes in bottle and magnum.

maurice-schoech.name: Maurice Schoech
maurice-schoech.line: A family estate in Ammerschwihr with grand cru vines in Kaefferkopf and nearby sites.
maurice-schoech.tell: Schoech is a family estate in Ammerschwihr. Kaefferkopf, Furstentum and Schlossberg are grand crus, and the wines are ripe and aromatic; ask the sommelier which carry sweetness.

lucien-crochet.name: Lucien Crochet
lucien-crochet.line: A family estate in Bué, in the heart of Sancerre, making crisp whites and fine Pinot Noir rosé.
lucien-crochet.tell: Lucien Crochet is a family estate in Sancerre. Their rosé is Pinot Noir: pale, dry and delicate, with red berries and citrus, offered in bottle and magnum, and very friendly with food.

chateau-clarke.name: Château Clarke
chateau-clarke.line: A Listrac estate owned by the Edmond de Rothschild family, making Merlot rich claret.
chateau-clarke.tell: Clarke is a Listrac estate owned by a branch of the Rothschild family. The magnum is good for a table.

chateau-cos-d-estournel.name: Château Cos d'Estournel
chateau-cos-d-estournel.line: A Saint-Estèphe second growth, known for its pagoda towered chai, making rich, exotic, polished Cabernet and Merlot blends.
chateau-cos-d-estournel.tell: Cos d'Estournel is the leading name in Saint-Estèphe, famous for its oriental style towers. The wine is rich and polished, more opulent than most of its neighbours. Decant younger vintages; the magnums are perfect for big celebrations.

chateau-cos-labory.name: Château Cos Labory
chateau-cos-labory.line: A Saint-Estèphe fifth growth neighbouring Cos d'Estournel, making classic, firm claret at fair prices.
chateau-cos-labory.tell: Cos Labory sits next door to Cos d'Estournel and gives classic Saint-Estèphe at a gentler price. The magnum is a fine pick for a table of four or more.

chateau-gombaude-guillot.name: Château Gombaude-Guillot
chateau-gombaude-guillot.line: A small family estate in Pomerol making Merlot led wine.
chateau-gombaude-guillot.tell: Gombaude-Guillot is a small family Pomerol. Soft, plummy Merlot. The several vintages here make for a good comparison.

chateau-lafite-rothschild.name: Château Lafite Rothschild
chateau-lafite-rothschild.line: The first growth of Pauillac owned by the Rothschild family since 1868, famous for its elegance and perfume.
chateau-lafite-rothschild.tell: Lafite is perhaps the most famous name in Bordeaux. It is a first growth known for elegance and fragrance rather than raw power. These are trophy bottles: involve the sommelier, decant, and let the moment breathe.

chateau-la-lagune.name: Château La Lagune
chateau-la-lagune.line: A Haut-Médoc third growth near Bordeaux city, making fragrant, fine claret.
chateau-la-lagune.tell: La Lagune is a third growth in the southern Médoc. Fragrant and fine. The magnum is good for a table.

chateau-palmer.name: Château Palmer
chateau-palmer.line: A Margaux third growth, farmed biodynamically, often priced beside the first growths, known for Merlot rich, perfumed, silky wine.
chateau-palmer.tell: Palmer is a third growth that often sells for close to first growth prices. Rich in Merlot, perfumed and silky. Historical XIX Century Wine is a special blend recalling an older Bordeaux custom; ask the sommelier about it.

chateau-saint-cosme.name: Château de Saint Cosme
chateau-saint-cosme.line: The historic Gigondas estate of Louis Barruol, making fine, spicy Gigondas and also a Châteauneuf-du-Pape.
chateau-saint-cosme.tell: Saint Cosme is the leading name in Gigondas. Their Gigondas is spicy and deep. The magnum is great for a big table.

clos-rougeard.name: Clos Rougeard
clos-rougeard.line: The cult Saumur-Champigny estate built by the Foucault brothers, making some of the most sought after Cabernet Franc in the world; now owned by Martin Bouygues.
clos-rougeard.tell: Clos Rougeard is a legend among Loire lovers. Le Clos, Les Poyeaux and Le Bourg are long lived, fine Cabernet Franc that collectors chase. These are rare bottles; decant and treat them like great Burgundy.

clos-saint-jean.name: Clos Saint Jean
clos-saint-jean.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine known for rich, ripe, powerful top cuvées.
clos-saint-jean.tell: Clos Saint Jean makes rich, powerful Châteauneuf. La Combe des Fous and Sanctus Sanctorum are their top cuvées. Big wines for big meats.

domaine-dujac.name: Domaine Dujac
domaine-dujac.line: The Morey-Saint-Denis domaine founded by Jacques Seysses and run by his family, known for whole cluster fermentation and silky, perfumed reds.
domaine-dujac.tell: Dujac is one of Burgundy's most loved names. They ferment with whole bunches, which gives a spicy, floral lift and silky texture; Dujac Fils et Père is the family's négociant label from bought grapes. From village wine to Clos de la Roche, these are elegant, fragrant bottles.

jean-paul-thevenet.name: Domaine Jean-Paul Thévenet
jean-paul-thevenet.line: One of the founding natural wine growers of Morgon, making old vine, fresh, deep Gamay.
jean-paul-thevenet.tell: Thévenet was one of the original natural growers of Morgon. The old vine Morgon in magnum is a fun pick for a big table.

domaine-du-pegau.name: Domaine du Pegau
domaine-du-pegau.line: The Féraud family's traditional Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine, known for powerful, savoury, old school Grenache; Château Pégau is a related family estate.
domaine-du-pegau.tell: Pégau is one of the most traditional names in Châteauneuf. Cuvée Réservée is the main wine; Cuvée Laurence spends longer in barrel. Big, savoury reds; large formats here are great for a big table.

marquis-d-angerville.name: Marquis d'Angerville
marquis-d-angerville.line: The great Volnay domaine, owner of the Clos des Ducs monopole, making pure, fragrant reds, farmed biodynamically.
marquis-d-angerville.tell: D'Angerville is perhaps the most famous name in Volnay. Clos des Ducs is their walled vineyard; Champans, Taillepieds and Caillerets are top premier crus. Elegant, fragrant and long lived.

domaine-ponsot.name: Domaine Ponsot
domaine-ponsot.line: A famous Morey-Saint-Denis domaine, a great name in Clos de la Roche, known for a traditional style without new oak and cuvées named after birds and insects.
domaine-ponsot.tell: Ponsot is one of the great Morey names, with grand crus from Clos de la Roche to Chambertin. Cuvée names like Grives, Pinson and Abeille mean thrush, finch and bee. The wines are fragrant and long; suggest decanting the grand crus.

domaine-de-la-romanee-conti.name: Domaine de la Romanée-Conti
domaine-de-la-romanee-conti.line: The most famous estate in Burgundy, sole owner of Romanée-Conti and La Tâche, with holdings in Richebourg, Romanée-Saint-Vivant, Échezeaux and Grands-Échezeaux.
domaine-de-la-romanee-conti.tell: DRC is the most celebrated wine estate in the world for many collectors. Romanée-Conti and La Tâche are wholly owned grand crus. These bottles are extremely rare; involve the sommelier for service, decanting and any questions about the vintage.

domaine-tempier.name: Domaine Tempier
domaine-tempier.line: The famous Bandol domaine of the Peyraud family, making Mourvèdre led reds from named sites.
domaine-tempier.tell: Tempier is the most famous name in Bandol. La Migoua and La Tourtine are single site wines; Lulu et Lucien is a special cuvée. Big, savoury reds for lamb.

gourt-de-mautens.name: Gourt de Mautens
gourt-de-mautens.line: A small Rasteau domaine, run by Jérôme Bressy, making deep, fine Grenache led wine sold under a regional name.
gourt-de-mautens.tell: Gourt de Mautens is a much admired small estate near Rasteau. Expect a deep, fragrant Grenache led wine. The magnum is great for a big table.

jean-foillard.name: Jean Foillard
jean-foillard.line: One of the original natural wine growers of Morgon, famous for the Côte du Py, making deep, fine, age worthy Gamay.
jean-foillard.tell: Foillard is one of the original Beaujolais growers who changed how the region is seen. Côte du Py is a famous hill in Morgon. The wines have depth and freshness; serve them slightly cool.

morey-coffinet.name: Domaine Morey-Coffinet
morey-coffinet.line: A family estate in Chassagne, organic and biodynamic in its farming.
morey-coffinet.tell: Morey-Coffinet is a family estate in Chassagne-Montrachet. En Remilly is a premier cru and Les Houillères a village site, with a Bâtard-Montrachet grand cru at the top and a Rully as the value bottle.

zind-humbrecht.name: Zind-Humbrecht
zind-humbrecht.line: A great biodynamic estate in Turckheim making rich, powerful whites.
zind-humbrecht.tell: Zind-Humbrecht is one of Alsace's leaders, with rich, powerful whites. Goldert is a grand cru, and this one is Muscat, aromatic and rich.

jules-desjourneys.name: Jules Desjourneys
jules-desjourneys.line: A Beaujolais grower making serious, structured cru wines, here Fleurie.
jules-desjourneys.tell: Desjourneys makes deep, structured Beaujolais that is priced more like Burgundy. Les Moriers is a Fleurie site. Ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

thierry-allemand.name: Thierry Allemand
thierry-allemand.line: A cult Cornas grower making tiny amounts of pure, deep Syrah from Chaillot and Reynard.
thierry-allemand.tell: Allemand is a cult name in Cornas. Les Chaillot is the fresher one; Reynard is deeper. Rare bottles; decant.

inglenook.name: Inglenook
inglenook.line: A historic Rutherford estate restored by Francis Ford Coppola, whose flagship red is Rubicon.
inglenook.tell: Inglenook is one of Napa's historic estates in Rutherford, brought back together by Francis Ford Coppola. Rubicon is the flagship Cabernet blend, deep and structured; Blancaneaux is the estate's white blend, rounder and richer.

chateau-latour.name: Château Latour
chateau-latour.line: The Pauillac first growth beside the Gironde, owned by the Pinault family, famous for powerful, long lived Cabernet.
chateau-latour.tell: Latour is the most powerful of the first growths, famed for consistency and longevity. The estate releases its wines only when it judges them ready. Decant, and serve with beef or lamb.

chateau-trotanoy.name: Château Trotanoy
chateau-trotanoy.line: A Pomerol estate of the Moueix family, making powerful, deep Merlot.
chateau-trotanoy.tell: Trotanoy is a Moueix Pomerol, powerful and deep. A great choice for a Pomerol lover.

chateau-canon.name: Château Canon
chateau-canon.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé on the limestone plateau, owned by the family behind Chanel, making fine, fresh wine.
chateau-canon.tell: Canon is a premier grand cru on the limestone plateau, owned by the family behind Chanel. Fine, fragrant and fresh.

chateau-figeac.name: Château Figeac
chateau-figeac.line: A Saint-Émilion estate on gravel, unusually rich in Cabernet, promoted to premier grand cru classé A in 2022.
chateau-figeac.tell: Figeac is unusual in Saint-Émilion for its high share of Cabernet. It was promoted to the top rank in 2022. Fine and long lived.

Selections Under $100.title: Selections under $100
Selections Under $100.line: The list's short page of bottles under $100, from sparkling to red. Start here for a guest who wants value: ask white or red, light or full, and point to one bottle in each.

Selections Under $100 ~ Sparkling.title: Sparkling under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Sparkling.line: Trento, English and Loire sparkling plus a Lambrusco: Champagne method bubbles at a friendly price, and a chilled sparkling red for the curious. Ask whether the guest wants dry and crisp or fruity.

Selections Under $100 ~ Sauvignon Blanc.title: Sauvignon Blanc under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Sauvignon Blanc.line: A white Graves and an Adelaide Hills Sauvignon Blanc: crisp, citrusy whites for oysters, salads and fish. Ask whether the guest likes zesty or rounder.

Selections Under $100 ~ Chardonnay.title: Chardonnay under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Chardonnay.line: Value Chardonnay from Burgundy, Oregon, California and Mendoza, with an Aligoté. Ask whether the guest wants crisp and unoaked or round and creamy, then pick Burgundy or California.

Selections Under $100 ~ Other White Vari.title: Other whites under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Other White Vari.line: Arneis, Pinot Grigio, Grüner Veltliner, Riesling, an Alsace blend and southern French bottles: aromatic, fresh and food friendly. Ask what the guest usually drinks and steer by aroma and weight.

Selections Under $100 ~ Rosé.title: Rosé under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Rosé.line: Two dry rosés, from the south of France and Santa Barbara: pale, crisp and good with almost anything on the menu. Easy to recommend to a table that cannot agree.

Selections Under $100 ~ Pinot Noir.title: Pinot Noir under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Pinot Noir.line: Bourgogne, Sonoma Coast and Victoria Pinot Noir: light to medium reds for fish, poultry and pork. Ask whether the guest likes earthy and fresh or ripe and fruity.

Selections Under $100 ~ Cabernet Sauvign.title: Cabernet under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Cabernet Sauvign.line: Napa, Bordeaux and Maipo Cabernet at friendly prices: dark, firm reds for beef. Duckhorn and Chappellet are names guests know; Massereau is mature Bordeaux.

Selections Under $100 ~ Other Red Variet.title: Other reds under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Other Red Variet.line: Montepulciano, Malbec, Gamay, Nebbiolo, Petit Verdot, Beaujolais and Grenache: a tour of good value reds. Ask light or full, then pick Gamay and Grenache for light, Malbec and Petit Verdot for full.

Half-bottles.title: Half-bottles
Half-bottles.line: 375 ml bottles, about two and a half glasses each: right for one or two guests or for a change of wine between courses. Ask how many are drinking and which course it is for.

Half-bottles ~ Champagne & Sparkling.title: Sparkling half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ Champagne & Sparkling.line: Krug, Laurent-Perrier, Feuillatte, Veuve Fourny, Ferrari and Schramsberg in half bottle. A perfect toast for two; the Laurent-Perrier Harmony is a sweeter demi-sec for dessert.

Half-bottles ~ White.title: White half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ White.line: Half bottles of white from France, Germany, Austria and California, dry and sweet. Ask whether it is for the meal or dessert: the Auslese Rieslings and the Huet Demi-Sec carry sweetness.

Half-bottles ~ White ~ France.title: French white half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ White ~ France.line: Vouvray Demi-Sec, Chablis Montmains, Meursault and Bourgogne Blanc. Chablis for oysters, Meursault for richer fish, and Huet when a touch of sweetness helps a spicy dish.

Half-bottles ~ White ~ Germany.title: German white half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ White ~ Germany.line: Auslese Rieslings from Dönnhoff, Dr. Hermann and Keller: sweet, bright and fine. Pour them with dessert, foie gras or blue cheese, or with a spicy dish.

Half-bottles ~ White ~ Austria.title: Austrian white half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ White ~ Austria.line: Schloss Gobelsburg Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from the Kamptal: dry, peppery or mineral whites for fish, vegetables and lighter courses.

Half-bottles ~ White ~ United States.title: American white half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ White ~ United States.line: A Sonoma Chardonnay and a Napa Viognier: round, ripe whites for a guest who likes California richness.

Half-bottles ~ Red.title: Red half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ Red.line: Half bottles of red from France, Italy, the United States and Argentina, from Beaujolais to first growth Bordeaux. Ask the budget and whether the guest wants light or full.

Half-bottles ~ Red ~ France.title: French red half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ Red ~ France.line: Burgundy, Bordeaux classed growths, Rhône and Beaujolais in half bottle. Mouton and Las Cases for a treat, Jadot Beaujolais-Villages for value, Gouges Nuits-Saint-Georges for beef.

Half-bottles ~ Red ~ Italy.title: Italian red half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ Red ~ Italy.line: Barbaresco from Gaja, La Spinetta and Ronchi, and Gaja's Magari from the Tuscan coast. Fragrant, firm Nebbiolo for beef and game.

Half-bottles ~ Red ~ United States.title: American red half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ Red ~ United States.line: Napa Cabernet and Merlot, Oregon and Sonoma Pinot Noir and Ridge Zinfandel. Opus One and Diamond Creek for a treat; La Crema or Bethel Heights for a lighter red.

Half-bottles ~ Red ~ Argentina.title: Argentine red half-bottle
Half-bottles ~ Red ~ Argentina.line: Catena Malbec: dark, ripe and smooth, a friendly half bottle for steak.

Large Formats.title: Large formats
Large Formats.line: Magnums and bigger, from 1.5 litres to a 15 litre Nebuchadnezzar. A magnum is two bottles; larger sizes need planning with the sommelier. Ask how many are at the table and what they are celebrating.

Large Formats ~ Champagne • Large Format.title: Champagne in large format
Large Formats ~ Champagne • Large Format.line: Champagne magnums and bigger, from house blends to Cristal, Salon and Dom Ruinart. A magnum serves a table of six to eight; Methuselahs and larger need the sommelier.

Large Formats ~ Sparkling • Large Format.title: Sparkling in large format
Large Formats ~ Sparkling • Large Format.line: Austrian sparkling magnums from Bründlmayer and Schloss Gobelsburg, made the Champagne way: crisp, elegant and good value for a big toast.

Large Formats ~ White • Large Format.title: White in large format
Large Formats ~ White • Large Format.line: Magnums of white from California, Austria, Germany and France. Ask how many are drinking and whether they like crisp or rich, then choose Chablis or Riesling for crisp, Meursault or Napa for rich.

Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ U.title: American white magnums
Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ U.line: Au Bon Climat, Far Niente and Mayacamas Chardonnay in magnum: from fresh Santa Barbara to rich Napa.

Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ A.title: Austrian white magnums
Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ A.line: Kamptal Riesling from Hirsch and Schloss Gobelsburg, and Gobelsburg's traditional Tradition. Dry, mineral and fine with seafood.

Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ G.title: German white magnums
Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ G.line: Dönnhoff and J.J. Prüm Riesling in magnum. Ask the sommelier which are dry and which carry sweetness before pouring.

Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ F.title: French white magnums
Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ F.line: Chablis, Meursault, Corton-Charlemagne, Alsace Riesling, Muscadet, Sancerre and Grange des Pères in magnum and larger. Muscadet and Chablis for oysters; Meursault and Corton-Charlemagne for richer dishes.

Large Formats ~ Rosé • Large Format.title: Rosé in large format
Large Formats ~ Rosé • Large Format.line: Sancerre and Provence rosé in magnum: pale, dry and a cheerful choice for a big table.

Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format.title: Red in large format
Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format.line: Red magnums and bigger from France, Italy, Spain and the United States. Ask the budget, the table size and whether they want Old World or New, then let the sommelier handle the decant.

Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Fra.title: French red magnums
Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Fra.line: Bordeaux classed growths, Burgundy grand crus, Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Bandol and Beaujolais in magnum and larger. From Morgon for fun to Romanée-Conti for a once in a lifetime night.

Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Ita.title: Italian red magnums
Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Ita.line: Barolo, Barbaresco, Brunello, Amarone and Super Tuscans in magnum, with Quintarelli and Oddero well represented. Firm, food loving wines for beef and game.

Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Spa.title: Spanish red magnum
Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Spa.line: Remelluri Gran Reserva Rioja in magnum: mature, savoury and fine, a lovely bottle for lamb.

Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Uni.title: American red magnums
Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Uni.line: Napa Cabernet from Opus One, BOND, Heitz and Spottswoode, Oregon and California Pinot Noir and more, in magnum and larger. Ask Cabernet or Pinot, and the budget.

Sustainable Selections.title: Sustainable selections
Sustainable Selections.line: Bottles from organic, biodynamic or natural growers, as the list marks each one. Questions about how a wine is made go to the sommelier; steer by style as with any other wine.

Sustainable Selections ~ White.title: Sustainable whites
Sustainable Selections ~ White.line: A Rully, a Bandol and an Alsace grand cru Muscat from organic, natural or biodynamic growers. Aromatic, textured whites for seafood and vegetables.

Sustainable Selections ~ Red.title: Sustainable reds
Sustainable Selections ~ Red.line: Natural, organic and biodynamic reds from Umbria, Etna, Friuli, Beaujolais, Cornas and Australia. Many are lighter and fresher than classic reds; ask whether the guest is adventurous.

Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red.title: Austria, Germany and Lebanon reds
Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red.line: Austrian Blaufränkisch and Pinot Noir, German Pinot Noir from the Pfalz and Château Musar from Lebanon. Fresh, peppery reds, with Musar as the spicy, mature exception.

Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Austr.title: Austrian reds
Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Austr.line: Blaufränkisch from Burgenland and Carnuntum and a Thermenregion Pinot Noir: fresh, peppery, dark cherried reds, a smart swap for a Burgundy or Rhône drinker.

Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Germa.title: German reds
Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Germa.line: Pfalz Pinot Noir from Lukas Hammelmann: fresh, red fruited and light. Suggest for fish, poultry or a guest curious about German red.

Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Leban.title: Lebanese reds
Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Leban.line: Château Musar from the Bekaa Valley, in several vintages: spicy, earthy and mature. Ask the sommelier which vintage is drinking best.

United States ~ Pinot Noir.title: American Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir.line: Pinot Noir from Mendocino, Sonoma, Santa Barbara, the Central Coast and Oregon. Ask whether the guest wants fresh and savoury or ripe and plush, then steer to Oregon or Kosta Browne style.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Mendocino.title: Mendocino Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Mendocino.line: Cool, foggy Anderson Valley and Mendocino hills: bright, fragrant Pinot Noir from Copain, Lioco, Maggy Hawk and others.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Sonoma Coas.title: Sonoma Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Sonoma Coas.line: Russian River, Sonoma Coast and Sonoma Valley Pinot: from plush Kosta Browne and La Crema to taut Hirsch and rare Marcassin. Ask ripe or restrained.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Napa Valley.title: Napa Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Napa Valley.line: A single Napa Valley Pinot Noir, from Brick & Mortar; ask the sommelier about its style.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Central Coa.title: Central Coast Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Central Coa.line: Santa Maria Valley, Sta. Rita Hills, Mount Harlan and Santa Lucia Highlands: Au Bon Climat, Calera and Domaine de la Côte for Burgundy lovers.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Oregon.title: Oregon Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Oregon.line: Willamette Valley Pinot Noir from Eyrie, Bergstrom, Ken Wright and others: fresh, red fruited and earthy, often a step towards Burgundy. Great with salmon and duck.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon.title: American Cabernet Sauvignon
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon.line: The deepest page of American red: Napa above all, with Sonoma, the Central Coast and Washington. Ask the budget and whether the guest wants plush and ripe or firm and classic.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Nap.title: Napa Cabernet
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Nap.line: Napa Cabernet from approachable to cult: Caymus and Duckhorn are friendly names, Heitz and Mayacamas classic, Harlan, BOND and Opus One for celebrations. Ask budget first, then ripe or restrained.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Son.title: Sonoma Cabernet
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Son.line: Alexander and Knights Valley Cabernet from Jordan, Silver Oak, Peter Michael and Vérité: often a little fresher than Napa. A good steer for a guest who wants balance.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Cen.title: Central Coast Cabernet
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Cen.line: Ridge Monte Bello from the Santa Cruz Mountains, DAOU from Paso Robles and a few others: firm and classic, or rich and modern.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Was.title: Washington Cabernet
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Was.line: Quilceda Creek and Andrew Will: dark, polished Cabernet with fresh acidity, a smart swap for a Napa drinker.

United States ~ Other ~ Red.title: Other American reds
United States ~ Other ~ Red.line: Syrah, Merlot, Zinfandel, Cabernet Franc, Petite Sirah and blends. Ask what the guest usually loves, then match: Merlot for plush, Syrah for peppery, Zinfandel for spicy and jammy.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Syrah.title: American Syrah
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Syrah.line: California, Oregon and Washington Syrah: cool climate bottles from Peay, Radio-Coteau and Ex Post Facto are peppery and savoury; Charles Smith and Shafer are bigger.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Merlot.title: American Merlot
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Merlot.line: Napa and Sonoma Merlot from Duckhorn, Pride, Keenan and Vérité: plush, plummy and soft. A good steer for a guest who finds Cabernet too firm.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Zinfandel.title: Zinfandel
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Zinfandel.line: Ridge, Radio-Coteau, Grgich and others: spicy, brambly reds, from fresh and light to ripe and jammy. Good with richer, spicier dishes.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Cabernet F.title: American Cabernet Franc
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Cabernet F.line: Cabernet Franc from Keenan, Vérité, Lang & Reed and Ancient Oak: fragrant, red fruited and lightly herbal. A swap for a Loire or Right Bank lover.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Petite Sir.title: Petite Sirah and friends
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Petite Sir.line: Dark, firm reds: Dunn from Howell Mountain and Stag's Leap Ne Cede Malis. Big wines for beef.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Unique Red.title: Unique American reds and blends
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Unique Red.line: Blends and unusual grapes: Nebbiolo, Gamay, Pinot Meunier, Malbec and Bordeaux style blends. A page for the curious; ask what they want to try.

Italy ~ Red.title: Italian reds
Italy ~ Red.line: Piedmont Nebbiolo, Veneto Amarone, Tuscan Sangiovese and Super Tuscans, and reds from the south and Sicily. Ask the region the guest likes, or light and fragrant versus rich and dark.

Italy ~ Red ~ Valle d'Aosta.title: Valle d'Aosta
Italy ~ Red ~ Valle d'Aosta.line: Alpine reds from the far north west: Grosjean Gamay, light and fresh.

Italy ~ Red ~ Piedmont ~ Barbaresco.title: Barbaresco
Italy ~ Red ~ Piedmont ~ Barbaresco.line: Nebbiolo from Barbaresco: fragrant, firm and often a little more graceful than Barolo. Produttori for value, Gaja and Giacosa for celebration, Roagna for tradition.

Italy ~ Red ~ Piedmont ~ Barolo.title: Barolo
Italy ~ Red ~ Piedmont ~ Barolo.line: Nebbiolo from Barolo: rose, tar and firm tannin, long lived. Ask the budget and whether the guest wants traditional or modern; older vintages from Bartolo Mascarello and Oddero need the sommelier.

Italy ~ Red ~ Other Piemonte & Lombardy.title: Other Piedmont and Lombardy reds
Italy ~ Red ~ Other Piemonte & Lombardy.line: Langhe Nebbiolo, Gaja single vineyards, Dolcetto, Barbera, and alpine Nebbiolo from Carema, Gattinara, Ghemme, Boca and Valtellina: lighter, fragrant cousins of Barolo.

Italy ~ Red ~ Alto Adige & Friuli-Venezi.title: Alto Adige and Friuli reds
Italy ~ Red ~ Alto Adige & Friuli-Venezi.line: Pinot Nero from Alto Adige and Merlot from Friuli: fresh, fine reds from the north east, good with fish and poultry.

Italy ~ Red ~ Veneto.title: Veneto reds
Italy ~ Red ~ Veneto.line: Valpolicella and Amarone, made partly from dried grapes: from fresh Verona reds to rich, deep Amarone from Quintarelli, Dal Forno, Masi and Bertani. Ask how rich the guest likes it.

Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ Chianti.title: Chianti
Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ Chianti.line: Sangiovese from Chianti and Chianti Classico: cherry, herbs and fresh acidity. Gran Selezione is the top tier. Great with tomato, veal and pasta.

Italy ~ Red ~ Vino Nobile di Montepulcia.title: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano
Italy ~ Red ~ Vino Nobile di Montepulcia.line: Sangiovese from the hill town of Montepulciano in Tuscany, firm and savoury.

Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ Brunello & Rosso.title: Brunello di Montalcino
Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ Brunello & Rosso.line: Sangiovese from Montalcino: deeper and longer lived than Chianti. Ask the budget; Biondi-Santi and Poggio di Sotto for classic finesse, Casanova di Neri for richness.

Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ IGT & Super Tusc.title: Super Tuscans
Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ IGT & Super Tusc.line: Tuscan reds outside the old rules, often with Cabernet or Merlot: Sassicaia, Tignanello, Solaia and Masseto. Rich and polished; a natural steer for a Napa or Bordeaux lover.

Italy ~ Red ~ Marche.title: Marche
Italy ~ Red ~ Marche.line: Rosso Piceno from Colleleva: Montepulciano and Sangiovese, juicy and great value.

Italy ~ Red ~ Umbria.title: Umbria
Italy ~ Red ~ Umbria.line: Sagrantino from Montefalco, one of the most tannic reds anywhere, and lighter natural reds. Decant the Sagrantino and serve it with braised meats.

Italy ~ Red ~ Abruzzo.title: Abruzzo
Italy ~ Red ~ Abruzzo.line: Emidio Pepe Montepulciano d'Abruzzo in several vintages: earthy, deep and traditional. Ask the sommelier which is ready.

Italy ~ Red ~ Campania.title: Campania
Italy ~ Red ~ Campania.line: Aglianico from Taurasi and Irpinia: dark, smoky and firm, the great red of the south. Good with lamb and beef.

Italy ~ Red ~ Sicily.title: Sicily
Italy ~ Red ~ Sicily.line: Etna Nerello Mascalese, fragrant and mineral like a southern Burgundy, plus Cerasuolo di Vittoria and Faro. Ask whether the guest likes light and fragrant reds.

Spain ~ Red.title: Spanish reds
Spain ~ Red.line: From Atlantic Galicia to Rioja, Priorat, Ribera del Duero, Gredos and the Canary Islands. Ask classic and oak aged or fresh and modern, then steer to Rioja or to Gredos and Galicia.

Spain ~ Red ~ Galicia.title: Galicia
Spain ~ Red ~ Galicia.line: Mencía and local grapes from steep Atlantic river slopes in Ribeira Sacra, Valdeorras and Ribeiro: light, fresh, peppery reds, a great swap for Pinot lovers.

Spain ~ Red ~ Rioja.title: Rioja
Spain ~ Red ~ Rioja.line: Tempranillo led reds from classic houses and new estates. Crianza is youngest, Reserva older, Gran Reserva longest aged. Ask whether the guest likes mellow and mature or fresh and fruity.

Spain ~ Red ~ Priorat.title: Priorat
Spain ~ Red ~ Priorat.line: Garnacha and Carignan from steep slate in Catalonia: deep, mineral and powerful. Big reds for lamb and beef.

Spain ~ Red ~ Penedes.title: Penedès
Spain ~ Red ~ Penedes.line: Torres Mas La Plana Cabernet and natural Sumoll from Els Jelipins: two very different Catalan reds.

Spain ~ Red ~ Castilla y Leon.title: Castilla y León
Spain ~ Red ~ Castilla y Leon.line: Ribera del Duero Tempranillo, including Vega Sicilia and Pingus, and fresh Bierzo Mencía. Ask rich and dark or fresh and floral.

Spain ~ Red ~ Toro.title: Toro
Spain ~ Red ~ Toro.line: Numanthia Termanthia: powerful old vine Tempranillo from a hot zone on the Duero.

Spain ~ Red ~ Madrid.title: Vinos de Madrid
Spain ~ Red ~ Madrid.line: Mountain Garnacha from west of Madrid: fresh, fragrant and light on its feet.

Spain ~ Red ~ Sierra de Gredos.title: Sierra de Gredos
Spain ~ Red ~ Sierra de Gredos.line: Granite mountain Garnacha from Comando G and Jiménez-Landi: fragrant and fine, often compared to Burgundy.

Spain ~ Red ~ Castilla-La Mancha.title: Castilla-La Mancha
Spain ~ Red ~ Castilla-La Mancha.line: Envínate Albahra from Almansa and Hand Work Garnacha: juicy, good value reds.

Spain ~ Red ~ Canarias.title: Canary Islands
Spain ~ Red ~ Canarias.line: Envínate reds from volcanic Tenerife: Listán Negro and Listán Prieto, light, smoky and fresh. Adventurous and very food friendly.

International - Red.title: International reds
International - Red.line: Reds from Greece, Portugal, Argentina, Chile, South Africa, Australia and New Zealand. Ask which grape the guest likes, then find it here: Malbec, Shiraz, Pinot Noir or Cabernet.

International - Red ~ Greece.title: Greek reds
International - Red ~ Greece.line: Xinomavro from Naoussa and a Meteora blend: firm, fragrant reds, a fun swap for a Nebbiolo lover.

International - Red ~ Portugal.title: Portuguese reds
International - Red ~ Portugal.line: Baga from Bairrada, Ramisco from sandy Colares and Alicante Bouschet from Alentejo: firm, characterful reds.

International - Red ~ Argentina.title: Argentine reds
International - Red ~ Argentina.line: Mendoza Malbec from Catena, Achával-Ferrer, Zuccardi and Viña Cobos, and a Cabernet: dark, ripe and smooth. A natural steak partner.

International - Red ~ Chile.title: Chilean reds
International - Red ~ Chile.line: Maipo Cabernet, Carmenère and cool Pinot Noir from Itata and the Atacama: good value and fresh.

International - Red ~ South Africa.title: South African reds
International - Red ~ South Africa.line: Pinotage, a Bordeaux blend and Sadie Columella: fresh, balanced reds from the Western Cape.

International - Red ~ Australia.title: Australian reds
International - Red ~ Australia.line: Barossa Shiraz from Penfolds, Torbreck and Amon-Ra, McLaren Vale Grenache and cooler Victorian Pinot and Syrah. Ask big and rich or fresh and light.

International - Red ~ New Zealand.title: New Zealand reds
International - Red ~ New Zealand.line: Central Otago and Marlborough Pinot Noir and a Hawke's Bay Cabernet Merlot: fresh and fine.

Selections from our Birth Year.title: Selections from our birth year
Selections from our Birth Year.line: Four great 1946 Bordeaux, from the year the restaurant was born: Latour, Trotanoy, Canon and Figeac. Rare, mature bottles for an anniversary or milestone; involve the sommelier for vintage, price and decanting.

Selections from our Birth Year ~ Wine.title: Birth year Bordeaux
Selections from our Birth Year ~ Wine.line: Mature 1946 first growth and Right Bank Bordeaux, from the house's birth year. Celebration bottles; let the sommelier present and decant.

Dessert Wines.title: Dessert wines
Dessert Wines.line: Sweet wines by the bottle and half bottle, from Sauternes to Vin Santo and icewine. Ask what the guest is eating: lighter fruit desserts like fresh wines, caramel and nuts like richer ones.

Dessert Wines ~ France.title: French dessert wines
Dessert Wines ~ France.line: Sauternes and Barsac, including Yquem and Climens, sweet Loire Chenin and a Jura half bottle. Honeyed and golden; lovely with bread pudding, fruit and blue cheese.

Dessert Wines ~ Canada.title: Canadian icewine
Dessert Wines ~ Canada.line: Inniskillin Cabernet Franc icewine: sweet, red berried and bright.

Dessert Wines ~ United States.title: American dessert wines
Dessert Wines ~ United States.line: Late harvest wines from Ridge, Grgich and Calera: sweet and fruity, in small bottles.

Dessert Wines ~ Italy.title: Italian dessert wines
Dessert Wines ~ Italy.line: Vin Santo, Torcolato, Moscadello, Pantelleria passito and Quintarelli's sweet wines: nutty, honeyed or apricot sweet. Ask the dessert, then match nuts with Vin Santo and fruit with Moscato.

Dessert Wines ~ Austria & Hungary.title: Austrian dessert wine
Dessert Wines ~ Austria & Hungary.line: Kracher Auslese from Burgenland: honeyed, fresh and fine with fruit desserts.

Fortified Wines.title: Fortified wines
Fortified Wines.line: Port, Madeira, Sherry and Rivesaltes. Ask dry or sweet: Manzanilla is dry and salty, Madeira tangy, Port rich and sweet. Vintage Ports need decanting.

Fortified Wines ~ France.title: French fortified wine
Fortified Wines ~ France.line: Riveyrac Rivesaltes: long aged sweet wine from Roussillon, nutty and caramel edged.

Fortified Wines ~ Madeira.title: Madeira
Fortified Wines ~ Madeira.line: Single cask Malvasia and Verdelho and a Verdelho solera: tangy, nutty and caramel edged, from medium dry to rich.

Fortified Wines ~ Spain.title: Sherry
Fortified Wines ~ Spain.line: Manzanilla, Pale Cream and an old Valdespino solera: from bone dry and salty to gently sweet.

Fortified Wines ~ Portugal.title: Port
Fortified Wines ~ Portugal.line: Vintage, Late Bottled Vintage, Colheita and Garrafeira Port from the great houses. Vintage Port needs decanting; LBV and tawny are ready to pour. Lovely with chocolate, pecan and blue cheese.
